## Alaska Orders Probe of Decoy Senate Candidate
Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered state police Thursday to [investigate an alleged effort](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb0TAs3E9MFSqvKXq1tHC8HBoCVjwmih_Xzn9hM5H9-qe-3lezjammLd3e0VDoSwZ7y0hEdbFJtu-bcNsCat1uGMmu5UcFiWU5lJwEIt1FG-4yM6bgKgQOjRynAAGDYPoLmYSw-RCsH3vJ7eGHuQE0sE0-hHUYNcumqNOChBSgFIvJ933IFWQSnip1-BYL9BHKvX0VWKmC4b0KDesJ1euXTIXor0xeGVqZmq2qzsUDsbU_FFSpOjaAZ42fDuSuVReqsfa-F7LitymhBt6jiGUStyVHH4a8j93puZGpT4YzNEzeJMwaj1KPXbV-P0eU4pNj6wX29XG9FxF__vyZtRvAAAA___1qolE) by the Democrat candidate to confuse voters in the state’s crucial Senate race, days before Tuesday’s midterm elections, and the Justice Department issued a wave of grand jury subpoenas. A _New York Times_ investigation revealed that operatives tied to Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign and a national party committee [searched voter rolls](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLEO2yAQhp8Gb0RwOMYZGLp4S9eO1tkcDi0GC4gjv31F8wjdful0n_7_-_Wcn-iDj9tP3MlUl-ZInxKoVsozBix_sFDEShlXOihW3FJ0MwgYuBRciRnX6k-aZWeNIwJSHRmpH0rdB3UX3csgybseF9SLVlKiVouyMIygh7F3o9CdNw0nhRJSKIDxNvS9kuAkCCuHxa2sF2R9Tfn2O_lYX-TClU7KtzXtXTCvWo_C1A8GE4MpXkcqtZ0YTA3MYJKi5QeD6V14G8hg-o7jWwPFlHnKlnLhR04L8eT4jvniB4WaAvKvA77ifqDfIm9P3NKaLm4x8vIOwZ8trBgtBgZTl409Pj4EXwbNerHt6MO_wvX_NJ8G_gYAAP__QUWSHA) for Alaskans named Dan Sullivan, the name of the Republican incumbent she is trying to unseat. Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg who has done very little campaigning, later landed on the four-way ballot. Peltola’s campaign and the committee have denied [recruiting the candidate](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u4yAQBeCnwR0RDPivoNjGXbbd0pqYwWaDAWGuo7z9lW8e4bYz0jn6zr_7fEcffFz_4k6mujRHeh2BaqUyY8DjiQdFrFRwoUyx4pqim0FAx6XgSsy4VH_SLBtrHBGQasjIflSq7VQrms3osdekNbRja1s9PpS1WjtEGHAkN_SNN1ecFEpIoQCGW6e1kuAkCCu7h1uYFmR9TeX2P_lYN3LhnU4qtyXtTTBbrflg6g-DicFUN9p8CNePwbSlnS4Rg2nBPaNfI4Opk4NQSvMPkO_-Sdx-xUB4vvmO5c0zhZoC8g-eHzn5QIUvGK231yWX9CAGU1OMzS8fgj-6nmmx7uh_ypv6uzlPA98BAAD__0ANitI), and Peltola called the Times report a distraction. President Trump wrote on Truth Social that Peltola engaged in “election fraud” and [should face consequences](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0Luu4yAQxvGnsTssLr4kBcU27rLtltYYBpsNBgSj-OTtj3zyCKce6a_5fv8eywN88HH7CwdqcmmJeNaARFgWCFCfUDECYQGDGSPBlqJbJJcjE5wpvoAh_8JFtFY7RImqRS2mu1LDqAbe7hqmCd1NKtOj5YKvSgyThFVM99tw5xZar6-c4IoLrqS8dWPfKyGdkNyKcXWm6TlaT6l0_5OPtKML7_TC0pl0tEHvRLk26k8j50bO53l2Ln1dM657I-ecgidvaiPnA8qbZQyUAjADRwa_RWbxqGwF80TLzBUmVs2OBzLnMVhWc_IBCzMQrbdAWNmHhn1s2IXDCuZUqC3a5tOH4Os4NT3fDvDh51H6He9Ly-8AAAD__6kCkwo). The Justice Department is separately suing to block certification if Sen. Sullivan narrowly loses.
## Economy Grows Along with Inflation
The economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, [faster than the 3.2%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2y2yAQx0-DOnmWRcJxoSIN3UubUrOGxSZB4MDaGt8-I1_hVfsrdv5fv7_WL0o5ldsv2niRWNfCe88swm2lTP0vdS4k3Mjzg4vQrZa4IqAdNYwGVvKSXrzqISyRGdkMvOjzxZjZmhmG-4LWBKvna5xm8Nqa6Akig57hEgGu85CWQ06DAQ0G8cfJTpPRGDVC0PYavZqAQ5LaTn9qKnLnmN_1xe3k6zbk5S7y6Mr8VOgUun3fT89OUgO9jweFrkttb4Vuq4WPy76Wuh10GCt0Gg6-KHTPPt7CY5R7amH896Qm3MZPWwovKp5H7pI2ElboLjjZSdsJ4KzQDW0Jjz3lnLo9qwluG6X8iSjfG_a14P8AAAD__zb0iUU) that economists expected, led by consumer spending, according to advance estimates. Inflation kept climbing in the meantime. The Federal Reserve’s [preferred inflation gauge](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb7bgQUgyMHTxlq4drWd4xLQYLPwUq39fOb_Q7UpXOlf3fD2mB6acyvMTV3Ic61To2DMxU5sw4_6DOxVkauhpo8L4rCVOIMH2SvZaTug5vWhSXXCRCEh35NT1rvXF6ovsFmfQGBtCsOoW70peoqEIiHOQdrbeX7vkTpySWiqpAW6DNUYriApkUHaOXhhJIXFtw3dNhReK-be-qA2-rl12C_O2C_0hYBQwHscx-DL7sxQwnmgBo5JnvgsYN099KjEjp1r6Rltt3O-0Ma0ztf79bFh4zV1zYTtSzmm3V2Hkc8WU35P8P1EvB38BAAD___U1ezo) rose 0.5% in September and 3.6% from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August, the Commerce Department announced Thursday. Core prices, which [leave out food and energy](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1yqzAQRp9GdDDSih9TqLgNnW-bklmLlb2JkBi0gfjtM_YrpP_mO3POx3W-IkdO9_-4kpOQ50RniSRC-4wRyxcWSii0o6eNkuA9pzCDhr42urZ6Ri980GyqxQUiIFuRM8NobdfbTlcPR7SE8YK27azFcWhh0SYEb0w3DH70umL3ujPaaqMtwKXp29YaCAb0Yvpb8KrVtLDkvfnMnORBIT7zQXvj81pF9xDZirL_FEwKpvM8m5B_bt-FE5Xy2iiYyOeU16eCqdAmtN5or98Sm6eaU4gonFO1u2U7OUYu_aBafV-R45sif2tzOPgNAAD__-tUeSg), were up 3.1% over the year. Goods prices rose 3.9% and services 3.5%, while the personal savings rate slipped to 3.8% of disposable income. The reports come the day after Federal Reserve officials [held their benchmark rate](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFupDAQxvGnMZ2RPTawV7jYuxPdpkmREg14AGeNjWwHtG8fkVdIPdJP8_0_HsMDnXdhecONTJnjEOjMnkqhNKDH_MRMAQslnGinUHCJYR5AQMul4EoMOBV30CAra2YiIFWRkd0fpZpWNaJazTgiaamx09TKrtNjA4iTbUB3QqqbrZy5OCmUkEIB3OpWayVhliCsbMd5YlqQdSWm-jO6UFaa_SselOopbpU3ayl7ZurOoGfQn-dZbzlcNwY9Bf6VGfTXKgZ9LCslBv1MlnvCgzJPWCjzXAjti2PmyyWHmLh3GfkU45NblzOFcgGY-P0Oy7Jt_5jq4-QsU___Xv3ozO-U9ioZu5_Oe5fbjmmxbOj8z6Pld3kPA98BAAD__xX1kC4) at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, with two dissenting in favor of an increase to fight inflation.
## Star Trek’s Patrick Stewart Dies at 86
Sir Patrick Stewart, the Shakespearean actor who became Captain Jean-Luc Picard on _Star Trek: The Next Generation_ , [died Wednesday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAURb8Gd4zgwTJ2QZHG3aZNaT3DY4YMNha8eHb_PnJ-IfWRju49vz6XT8wl74-fuJHnVJed3r0QM7UFC_YXdtqRqWGgg3bGR93TAgqc1EoatWDgfNKih-gTEZAZyOv7ZMyHMx9qePpkYRyn0aWkIk1rSvdgXbRx1SGYie5D9pdOK6O0MgDjzVlrNCQNKmq3piCsopi5ttvvmnd-Uirf9aR2C3Ubin8yH12YHwJmAfOJLRN_X0zAfJkFzHwKmOua-c9FuzyoHoXk9VXAfCC3HF6yM72xsYyEUXbGJrnRSx45YItfcqNdfuGZqUkNxk3GWg0C5qH5eLxzKbm7u7DqsWEu_7bx_xU9PfwNAAD__yWgivQ) at his home in Los Angeles. He was 86. His family said he had Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, calling his illness “a brief and poignant journey” and remembering him as a figure of “invincible grace.” His wife, Sunny Ozell, was at his side. Born in a Yorkshire mill town, Stewart spent decades with the Royal Shakespeare Company and won [three Olivier Awards](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO6yAQgOHTmI4IBkziguI17vLaLa0JDDEbYiwYOcrtV9krbP1LX_F_XZcr5pK3-398kudUl41evRAztQUL9gd22pCpYaCdNsZ73dICCpzUShq1YOB80KJF9IkIyAjy-jwZMzozKrH6KYIbQYUYyGiyE7o4xmQd2XCeUAWR_YfTyiitDMDl5Kw1GpIGFbW7pTBYRTFzbafvmjdeKZV3PaidQn2K4lfmvQ_m3wDzAPNe8H3LpXziADM2zqHQAPONSj0oSgxcm9yRWw4P2Zle2Fiu2GXMn8zy4kTzcX_lUnJ358Gq-xPzryj4b5MODz8BAAD__4k-fKs) before taking command of the Starship Enterprise in 1987 for seven seasons, then playing Professor X across seven _X-Men_ films. He was knighted in 2010. He is survived by Ozell and his children, Sophie and Daniel. **A Note from Cole, CEO of _The Flyover_** Dear Reader, Every year, auditors count how many copies America's biggest newspapers actually put in people's hands. The new numbers are brutal. Of the 25 largest papers in the country, 24 shrank last year. Average decline: 12.5%. Nearly a quarter-million daily papers, gone in a single year. _The Denver Post_ now prints about 24,000 copies a day. _The Arizona Republic_ , 33,000. _The Houston Chronicle_ , 35,000. _The Dallas Morning News_ , under 40,000. These are metros of millions. And the steepest collapse in the country belonged to _The Washington Post_ : down 21% in a single year to fewer than 88,000 print copies. The industry will tell you it's the internet. It's a convenient story, because it means none of this is their fault. Here's the story they won't tell: Americans didn't stop caring about the news. They stopped trusting the people delivering it. Somewhere along the way, the papers stopped reporting what happened and started campaigning for what they wanted to happen--and their readers noticed. Trust in the media now sits at the lowest level ever recorded. So no, that's not an audience drifting away. That's a jury coming back with a verdict. Today’s sponsor, , helps you look beyond your weight with the Body Pod, an at-home scale that tracks body composition, including estimated body fat and muscle mass. | Alaska Orders Probe of Decoy Senate Candidate Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered state police Thursday to by the Democrat candidate to confuse voters in the state’s crucial Senate race, days before Tuesday’s midterm elections, and the Justice Department issued a wave of grand jury subpoenas. A New York Times investigation revealed that operatives tied to Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign and a national party committee for Alaskans named Dan Sullivan, the name of the Republican incumbent she is trying to unseat. Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg who has done very little campaigning, later landed on the four-way ballot. Peltola’s campaign and the committee have denied , and Peltola called the Times report a distraction. President Trump wrote on Truth Social that Peltola engaged in “election fraud” and . The Justice Department is separately suing to block certification if Sen. Sullivan narrowly loses. Economy Grows Along with Inflation The economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, that economists expected, led by consumer spending, according to advance estimates. Inflation kept climbing in the meantime. The Federal Reserve’s rose 0.5% in September and 3.6% from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August, the Commerce Department announced Thursday. Core prices, which , were up 3.1% over the year. Goods prices rose 3.9% and services 3.5%, while the personal savings rate slipped to 3.8% of disposable income. The reports come the day after Federal Reserve officials at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, with two dissenting in favor of an increase to fight inflation. Star Trek’s Patrick Stewart Dies at 86 Sir Patrick Stewart, the Shakespearean actor who became Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation , at his home in Los Angeles. He was 86. His family said he had Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, calling his illness “a brief and poignant journey” and remembering him as a figure of “invincible grace.” His wife, Sunny Ozell, was at his side. But I have to tell you that nothing is guaranteed. And over the last few days, Mike Lawler and his allies have been seriously outraising us. This is going to be a really brutal fight for every single vote until the very end.

## GOP Suit Seeks Statewide Hand Count
The Potter County Republican Party [filed a federal lawsuit](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp_GdCD_4RsXLrahy7ZbIseehJGMHdkDhLdfkVe49Rwdnfn-3ee7x4T59dev4OjzLHOGoyUggjqH4sPS_A6t0RYhE5UalrPlWXJpesF7xWcfCHeYte-ie_BoRQdO_FilxpswY7c4MJLryIUAbW6jHkdhrVYimqCsssZ06C6d4IoLwaWWg_U-PozVAaSOegxMc4hIpQ60AMHHt2c6yw51CGXtkluI3o2pP0xOTE7HcQzXE9kTlpzLcVFMTu-SkDA0Jqdv_oqRoK49JAgXeR2-8j75o21I_eJz7EPZMvXhfEBtELaKdDI5ddXF94EpYTM_TPPX6jF9c-i3M-5O_g8AAP__yiGKQQ) Tuesday to block Texas from certifying the Nov. 3 election until every paper ballot statewide is counted by hand, a request now before federal Judge Matthew Kacsmaryk, a Trump appointee. Chairman Daniel Rogers and the party argue that foreign-made voting machine parts and rogue AI programs could alter results without detection. Texas already requires a partial hand-count audit when machines are used, but the suit says that isn't enough. The complaint doesn't claim that any Texas machine was ever hacked or that votes were changed. University of Houston law professor David Froomkin called the case "weak" and [expects it to be dismissed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO8yAUBODT4A4LHtiJC4q_cZe_3dIi8ByQCFjwbCe3XyVX2HqkTzPzc1tuNqaYH__tEw291rJkPFtCIqyLK9aFZg9sjXaPmahUF94tLyBg5FJwJRbrKB64aNt5cxd-kh0aeZmUGq5yHLpglJIXFIMaRq-GUa4CnYUrgHa4CjlNXTQfTgolpBSgoZ-s9fdx0g5Bez04pgX6SKX2FJDwZdua3uXA2rvy7JIJRFtj6h-DmcF8nmfvQi35kzKYP4MYzLZSdAkZzF-BV9z2e4rO5sbbjjzY7LkreyaOCR3FkhsHGIQYJ9VvYeuq8dsZU4ptvDAtHk8b07cB_fW5w8BvAAAA___rpISw), saying the plaintiffs offer "nothing but wild conjectures."
## Silsbee Coach Saves Student
A Silsbee Middle School coach [performed the Heimlich maneuver](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkb_OnDAQxJ_GdHsya8yfgiIN3Zc2JVrWy2HF4JPtD-7ePrpTivRpZ0Yj_WZ-fc1f5IM_7j9pl7E81zgfcuUgpUiaORJvmU7JuXw7OUqJibdXPmbU2EKtweiZuPhT5oYqNy7aDXUlY90Nxti-bm21jWg1iXaLNSzDyoyLaVEsus6R4bqv_Piuq7XRda2xwdtA5JZ2aFiwcY1l1WhxvsR0K5sUeVJewyuekm4c9yqMWymPrMwPhZPC6bquW41vjCNe74TCiVLxHETh9NYVTiEyBYVT9iEvIrB754JA5i3GAB9weEhaY9ozbOL34HmDnQ75PiVBPIC3-Nsfd_g7DTxikaN4CuEFmc5_rAzBrwLlqXCyGqG3NLBeGLBFB01nNfS9bsGKYGOca43rqjS6x-VD8LntVKPvO_nwwS3_e9M54p8AAAD__yViqwI) on a choking student this week, clearing the airway and possibly saving the student's life, the district said in a Facebook post. The coach, Morgan Robberts, graduated from Silsbee High School in 2020 and is a [former All-State offensive lineman](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1ygzAQhU8jOnmkRYApVKShc9qUjJAWaycCeVgZ27fP4OQGKfdn3rzv-7qMF0eJ1uunW9CW55zHFR-csBTcRp-dj-x2ZC73gGspefPxxesIClqplazV6HyhHUfjqmAnFXpdodVdX9fNWbdNFW3nsKnPtZrrHhvQYKbOt9gqaLU69hVZ-B2U1goMnHrnwtT2xiOYYBovjMJAJW-nErHg0_GcXnnH7eTzUiUbS7mxqD8EDAKG7zksx0HAcLAIGFL2LgkYmBJPiPLNJf12hGKQDypR3pnWq4xISyIf5eJWvO-4yVtmpim9JLv9-PgzwTLRjNVmw-1BKRG3nTDqujhK71LlvzJ3Cz8BAAD__3Z-jUE). He returned to the district to teach and coach, working alongside the staff who had once coached him. "_Not all heroes wear capes_ ," the district wrote, thanking Robberts for his "quick thinking, calm demeanor, and life-saving actions." Robberts said he "was praying the whole time" and thanked God for having "his hand over the whole situation."
## Rain Soaks Texas Ahead of Halloween
Tropical Storm Vance's leftovers and Gulf moisture are spreading rain across Texas through the weekend, but forecasters from Dallas to Houston say [Halloween won't be a washout](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykULGu6yAU-xqyEQEhNBkY3pLtvvWN0SmcFCQSKjgN7d8_pb9wN8uWLdv_ftYfiCkej7-wo6X3ltcDW01IhGV1GVyocGKt9PJ4EOXiwqceqxLKcCn4IFZwFE9cNXTe3oWfZYdW3uZhGCdpxi5YPYATg9omJ6QfhR9HI_BmzKRxhElAF-0VJ8UgpBRKq34G8Hcza4dKez06pgX6SLn0FJDwDXVLn3xi6V3eu2QD0bOy4Q9TC1NLa61393rtuHSmlq-FqeWimFo8pASVNwQKWDhlDx8eIKXcEA--5YIOKl2AeMuFAifcn1iAXgUrz464mplaumL9s8WUYjU3psVjh5i-nei3X55W_Q8AAP__eBmM0A). West Texas gets the heaviest rain. Forecasters in Midland expect remnants of Vance to [stall over the region](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAUhJ8GOpB_cShc3CZdbrslOtjHsSUHI_ssJG-_Spp9gC1nRvpG-r5uyw1STtv9PzzQ0jOUZcOzZSTCurgCLjY4sDX69rgRleriq22LYGIaOBskW8BROnBR0Hu7Mj_zHi03s5T6wifdR6uCNI47pVzQMsAKAlc9G-NNuAgdpj7ZN44zyThnQolxBvDrNCuHQnmlXacY-kSljhSR8Akt5Fc5sI6uPPpsI9HeOvmvE9dOXM_zHF2sZXuv74xAEWsnrlApuYy_3RBKRQeNhg91iJBzORG3QQg1G6n1uMe9r9bvZ8o5tcl0it0fkPLnmv6q7LDiJwAA__9pvoMu) by Friday, dropping up to 6 inches in isolated spots and causing flash flooding in low-lying and urban areas. In North Texas, showers and a few thunderstorms build Friday afternoon ahead of the evening commute and linger into Saturday morning. Rain is expected to clear out from west to east by afternoon, leaving [a dry window for trick-or-treaters](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3uozAQxU8DnZFtDAmFi23SZdst0cQzxNYaO7InEG6_Itob_Nufnt7Xn_t8hxBDev6GlSx_ljwn2mskZiqzy-B8hY1q5TdSYs7F-aOmWUs9CiVFL2dwHDaaDbRoHxIn1ZJVl6nvh6sah9ZbowbspTQTXiSBcyOhvCLSuGg5DcvYBnvaKdlLpaQ2upsA8DFOxpE2aAbXGEkYOJeOPTF9oC7xyBuVzuW1jdYzv2rT_2r0rdG3fd-7JX_MOeQUnIiAPZVG3xBihCr-A1EgJOE8JEdVFOJ3SSLlwl58Y4SHGPNOlETM-W8Va64cD4HlaIvF1x5iDHW8NEY-Vwjx24d_-uNm9b8AAAD__2A9jQk). The Houston area expects a muggy Halloween with highs in the upper 70s to upper 80s and [scattered daytime storms possible](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D3uozAUBPDTmM6Rv8ChcLEN3X_bLdHDfsSWDI7sFwi3XyXSnmDr-Wk0mj8_8w-knPbHb9jQ0Xst845ny0iEdfYFfGxwYGv0CrgTlerj1fZZCTVwKbgWM3hKB84GuuAWEUbZoZN21Lq_y6HvorMWpJWrHXu7-MWKcF-CNlZp2w96sfcuuU-dFFpIKZRRtxEgLMNoPCoTTO-ZERgSlXqjiIRvaGu-yoH15svWZReJno3pX0xNTE1f0KjUzUdoWNtHMTWtpaKHRkxNV3lV_nU8Qs7lRNz5v5w_86vxiHBcvELa-YmNeFl54rpnauqqC88z5ZzaYJkRjw1S_i6h_33wcOpvAAAA__8ydokh), though the evening looks fine for most. Early next week, a cold front could bring strong storms to Houston and North Texas Monday night into Tuesday.

**A Note from Cole, CEO of _The Flyover_** Dear Reader, Every year, auditors count how many copies America’s biggest newspapers actually put in people’s hands. The new numbers are brutal. Of the 25 largest papers in the country, 24 shrank last year. Average decline: 12.5%. Nearly a quarter-million daily papers, gone in a single year. _The Denver Post_ now prints about 24,000 copies a day. _The Arizona Republic_ , 33,000. _The Houston Chronicle_ , 35,000. _The Dallas Morning News_ , under 40,000. These are metros of millions. And the steepest collapse in the country belonged to _The Washington Post_ : down 21% in a single year to fewer than 88,000 print copies. The industry will tell you it’s the internet. It’s a convenient story, because it means none of this is their fault. Here’s the story they won’t tell: Americans didn’t stop caring about the news. They stopped trusting the people delivering it. Somewhere along the way, the papers stopped reporting what happened and started campaigning for what they wanted to happen—and their readers noticed. Trust in the media now sits at the lowest level ever recorded.
So no, that’s not an audience drifting away. That’s a jury coming back with a verdict. And here’s the part the industry really doesn’t want to talk about: those readers didn’t give up on news. They went looking for someone who would just tell them the truth. Millions of them found their way to _The Flyover_ —a morning news publication built on one simple deal: We call things what they are. We keep the spin out and trust you with the facts. And _The Flyover_ stays free. It turns out that when you just give people the facts and trust them to think for themselves, people respond. body:
We’re going all in these last 4 days.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, weeks ago, the experts said Greg Abbott had this race locked up.
Today is the last day of early voting, and more than 6,000,000 Texans have already cast their ballots, and the projections based on who’s actually showing up tell a very different story:_**this race is neck and neck.**_
You made that happen. The ads, the texts, the doors our organizers knocked to bring voters to the polls — your support powered every bit of it.
For years, Abbott and his allies have tried to convince Texans that change here is impossible. **The early voting numbers are the clearest sign yet that they’re wrong.**
But we didn’t get into this race to come close. We got into it to win. And winning means bringing out even more voters: Texans who stayed home last time, and Texans who are still making up their minds. After today, there’s only one chance left to reach them: **Election Day, Tuesday, November 3rd.**
So we’re going all in. Our organizers will be knocking doors from now until polls close on Election Day, and we’re putting every dollar we have into ads and texts that reach voters before they head to the polls. Abbott can outspend us — but he can’t outwork us.
I know you haven’t given to our campaign yet. Maybe it felt like winning was out of reach — but not anymore. The early vote numbers prove it isn’t. Gina

name: Christi Heun
subject: Speak Up: The Trump admin wants to sacrifice 23 million acres of Arctic wildlife habitat.
body:
Stop this assault on the Arctic and the irreplaceable wildlife who call it home.

Stop this assault on the Arctic and the irreplaceable wildlife who call it home.
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6225195/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6225196/38SyG9Xl)

Act Now to Protect the Arctic (https://support.defenders.org/s/6225197/38SyG9Xl)

Defender,

Imagine half of Southern Beaufort Sea polar bears... just gone. This fragile population of polar bears has seen their population decline by nearly 50% as sea ice, essential for their survival, melts away.

Now, the Trump administration is proposing to end critical environmental reviews and fast-track oil and gas drilling across 23 million acres of public lands in Alaska's Western Arctic. This move threatens the fragile snow dens where polar bear mothers give birth and shelter their vulnerable cubs.

We only have until November 9 to make our voices heard. Click here to sign a message to Stevan Pearce, Director of the Bureau of Land Management: We will not stand by while you fast-track dangerous oil and gas development in the Western Arctic! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6225198/38SyG9Xl)

Take Action: Protect Arctic Wildlife! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6225199/38SyG9Xl)

Polar bears aren't the only species at risk. The Western Arctic is home to hundreds of thousands of caribou, snowy owls and millions of migratory birds who depend on its vast tundra and wetlands.

This proposal is another example of the administration's efforts to open the irreplaceable Western Arctic to industrial oil development — even as climate change pushes the wildlife who call it home closer to the brink of extinction.

The public comment deadline is November 9. There is little time left to make your voice heard.

Send your message now! We must stop the Trump administration and Big Oil from creating new laws at the cost of America’s wildlife and wild places. (https://support.defenders.org/s/6225200/38SyG9Xl)

Sincerely,

Christi Heun

Senior Representative, Alaska

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

 

 
Photo Credit: Polar Bears © Susanne Miller/USFWS

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com (mailto:dpwillis67@gmail.com)

body:
Three amendments are on your Tennessee ballot, and my guest Rep. Vincent Dixie and I are voting NO on every one.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/d89bf49f70d3/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363988?e=dc5f639d62)

Hey friends,Three amendments are on your Tennessee ballot, and my guest Rep. Vincent Dixie and I are **voting NO** on every one.
[CLICK HERE to LISTEN NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/yYbXWkaeu22?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/_xpcLGHhCSd?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**
Here’s the thing: the language you’ll see in the voting booth won’t tell you the whole story. Rep. Dixie of Nashville knows the bail system inside and out. He owns a bail bonding company, and he’s upfront about that, so you’ll hear it straight from someone who’s seen it up close.We dig into Amendment 1 and what it could mean for people who are accused but not convicted, for your county jail, and for your tax bill. We break down Amendment 2, the state property tax ban, and Amendment 3, the victims’ rights amendment. And we get into why policy doesn’t belong in our state’s Constitution.Your phone has probably been blowing up with questions about these. **Send this to someone who’s voting this week.****Here’s a quick look at why we’re voting NO:**
* **Amendment 1** takes away the right to bail for people accused of 73 felonies. That could mean months in jail before trial, and your county’s taxpayers footing the bill.
* **Amendment 2** bans a state property tax Tennessee doesn’t have. It won’t change your tax bill, and it limits what future lawmakers can do.
* **Amendment 3** adds victims’ rights to the Constitution that are already in state law and may affect due process rights.

**Early voting ends THIS Thursday, October 29** and Election Day is November 3. [**Find your polling location here**](https://us.list-manage.com/12mOnIQvFlR?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0).
Thank you for being here,
Gloria

Donald Trump is going through it.
He is staring down a cataclysmic loss on Tuesday. Democrats are now favored to win back the Senate, and it has him completely unraveling.
One of the states paving the path for Dems to retake the Senate is none other than Alaska, where Dem Mary Peltola has been leading in recent polls against MAGA's Dan Sullivan.
So naturally, the President of the United States is now demanding that Alaska's Senate election be canceled, all because another man named Daniel J. Sullivan is on the ballot:

Our president is off his rocker. It will only get more insane from here. And somehow, it will get even worse after he loses.

After the Ball: How America Will Conquer Its Fear and Hatred of Gays in the 90's (Doubleday) opens with the sentence no movement strategist is supposed to write: "The gay revolution has failed." From there, Marshall Kirk, a neuropsychiatry researcher, and Hunter Madsen, a public-relations consultant, diagnose why -- parades and slogans had failed -- and prescribe what would win instead: advertising. Kirk was dead by 1990, cause never publicly disclosed. The book he left behind ran the country for the next thirty-six years.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/806107ee-3f95-46cd-988f-abb79605336e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This was not a manifesto of grievance; it was a marketing plan. It grew out of a February 1988 war conference of 175 activists at Warrenton, Virginia, and out of a November 1987 article the pair published in Seattle's Guide magazine under the pen name Erastes Pill -- "The Overhauling of Straight America." Its stages had the romance of a spreadsheet: Desensitize. Jam. Convert...

From there, Marshall Kirk, a neuropsychiatry researcher, and Hunter Madsen, a public-relations consultant, diagnose why -- parades and slogans had failed -- and prescribe what would win instead: advertising. | | Hello my Friend, As we mark 250 years since the Declaration of Independence, it’s worth asking: **_[What did 1776 really mean—and why does it still matter today?](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc2K2zAUhZ9G3tnox5bshRdDnbSzyJQ2A0NXRtW9cS7IkrDktI9fDJMX6Pa7l-_AOR-X-WLJU1je7Ioj5TxDhBn_Jh83LHe8xT0AhSVtFBylWXKpa8FrxWfrCj1wbm0FYydFf-srHIUZlNKiF311HxWqDnmnWjXg4PStA2cAOo1db21rflc0Hj7BFReSK84b1NBZY90A2jkDnLV8T2ALNhQyAWYXY0rRUyGXm7gtlR_vpaTM1AuTZybPFG6xuZP3GazHBmFn8iyM0bVztn4QYKwzboSZqXPGZcVQvkRApibOBZdvXLby9eswfZ9OpyuTei_rnOO-ueMlbTEndIXC8nlaEWhfmZpwteQ_obNrsrQEpqYj-kljKBgKU9PHt1-Xl_f308_5h6lfr9f6WUO1jZD-kPeUtWEtXw5p4-Jalf8d5zHKfwEAAP__e4aeog)_** Hillsdale College has created a FREE video lecture series titled **“1776”** that explores these and other questions. It takes a thoughtful look at the ideas, events, and debates surrounding the Declaration of Independence and the American Revolution. **You can receive instant access to this free video series about 1776 today using this secure link:** [https://info.hillsdale.edu/1776-cca-video-series](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc2K2zAUhZ9G3tnox5bshRdDnbSzyJQ2A0NXRtW9cS7IkrDktI9fDJMX6Pa7l-_AOR-X-WLJU1je7Ioj5TxDhBn_Jh83LHe8xT0AhSVtFBylWXKpa8FrxWfrCj1wbm0FYydFf-srHIUZlNKiF311HxWqDnmnWjXg4PStA2cAOo1db21rflc0Hj7BFReSK84b1NBZY90A2jkDnLV8T2ALNhQyAWYXY0rRUyGXm7gtlR_vpaTM1AuTZybPFG6xuZP3GazHBmFn8iyM0bVztn4QYKwzboSZqXPGZcVQvkRApibOBZdvXLby9eswfZ9OpyuTei_rnOO-ueMlbTEndIXC8nlaEWhfmZpwteQ_obNrsrQEpqYj-kljKBgKU9PHt1-Xl_f308_5h6lfr9f6WUO1jZD-kPeUtWEtXw5p4-Jalf8d5zHKfwEAAP__e4aeog) In six engaging lectures, scholars walk through the principles and turning points that shaped our nation’s founding—along with the military, economic, and moral dimensions of the Revolution. **These are the topics you’ll explore:**
* The story of the Declaration of Independence
* Lexington and Concord
* The economics of the Revolution
* Keys to American victory
* Sermons of the Revolutionary era
* The ongoing debate over 1619 and 1776

For more than 50 years, Hillsdale has hosted a lecture series aimed at encouraging serious, civil discussion about the most important questions facing our country. We call the program the “Center for Constructive Alternatives.” **At a time when the meaning of 1776 is often misunderstood or rejected altogether, this free series offers a clear, historically grounded perspective on America’s founding.** **You can receive instant access to this free video series about 1776 using this secure link:** [https://info.hillsdale.edu/1776-cca-video-series](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc2K2zAUhZ9G3tnox5bshRdDnbSzyJQ2A0NXRtW9cS7IkrDktI9fDJMX6Pa7l-_AOR-X-WLJU1je7Ioj5TxDhBn_Jh83LHe8xT0AhSVtFBylWXKpa8FrxWfrCj1wbm0FYydFf-srHIUZlNKiF311HxWqDnmnWjXg4PStA2cAOo1db21rflc0Hj7BFReSK84b1NBZY90A2jkDnLV8T2ALNhQyAWYXY0rRUyGXm7gtlR_vpaTM1AuTZybPFG6xuZP3GazHBmFn8iyM0bVztn4QYKwzboSZqXPGZcVQvkRApibOBZdvXLby9eswfZ9OpyuTei_rnOO-ueMlbTEndIXC8nlaEWhfmZpwteQ_obNrsrQEpqYj-kljKBgKU9PHt1-Xl_f308_5h6lfr9f6WUO1jZD-kPeUtWEtXw5p4-Jalf8d5zHKfwEAAP__e4aeog) I hope you’ll take a few moments to watch and reflect on the principles, people, and events that shaped our nation—especially during this historic anniversary year. It's easy to win an argument when everyone in the room already agrees with you.
But we cannot keep talking exclusively to one another and expect the rest of the country to understand what we believe--or why.
_**[I 've decided to step into the arena.](https://substack.com/redirect/5bfe0cf1-eb1c-4ce6-9116-8fb187680759?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5bfe0cf1-eb1c-4ce6-9116-8fb187680759?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_To enter spaces outside our bubble. To explain our positions, defend our principles, answer difficult questions, and challenge assumptions about who we are.
Today, that work takes me to **BBC World Service 's Newshour at Midtown Scholar Bookstore in Harrisburg**, for a conversation focused on Pennsylvania's midterm elections and what our commonwealth may reveal about the direction of the nation.
**Come out, listen, and show your support.**
And I'm also asking you to help me keep doing it.

If a paid subscription isn't possible right now, come out today. Share this invitation. Forward my work to someone who might never otherwise hear this perspective.
You don't have to agree with every word I say to believe that our positions deserve a thoughtful, forthright voice in the conversation.
**I 'm willing to step into the arena. I hope you'll stand with me.**

subject: The last blue wave skipped Ohio. Not this time.

body:
A nickel a message, and 4 days to go

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/6d1NPxI6uuJ?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
| | | | | | Hello Peter,

I want to start with a simple thank you.
When I asked for help with our digital ads and text campaigns, you stepped up.
Because of you, our message is reaching voters across Ohio’s 8th District who too often get overlooked. That matters, and I don’t take it for granted.
But here’s what keeps me up at night: **the last time there was a blue wave in this country, it skipped Ohio.** We cannot let that happen again. We can’t get complacent, and we can’t take our foot off the gas. Not now, with Election Day just four days away.
**Here’s where we stand, and where you can make the biggest difference:**
**1\. Help us send 103,000 more text messages.**
We still need to reach rural and apartment voters, two communities that traditional campaigns often miss. Reaching all of them costs just **$5,166**. That’s about **five cents a message** , the most affordable way to put our message directly in voters’ hands. Every gift, of any size, gets us closer.

---
| [Chip in now](https://us.list-manage.com/BWKgTlzftUY?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
---
| |

**2\. Drop literature in your community.**
We need volunteers to drop lit in about 10 communities across Butler and Hamilton Counties this weekend. A few hours of your time can put our message on hundreds of doorsteps.
**3\. Place signs at polling places on Monday night.**
The night before the election, we need help placing signs at polling places across Hamilton County, so ours is one of the first names voters see when they arrive Tuesday morning. If you can give an hour or two on Monday evening, we’d love your help.

**4\. Call voters and remind them to vote.**
We need phone bankers to call voters and remind them to get to the polls. A friendly reminder from a real person can be the difference between someone meaning to vote and actually voting. You can make calls from home and from anywhere in the US, on your own schedule, and we’ll give you everything you need to get started.
---
| [Volunteer](https://us.list-manage.com/7Wx9Y7sA8eq?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
---
| |

**5\. Celebrate with us on Election Night.**
After all the hard work, I want us together when the results come in. Please make a plan to join our Election Night Watch Party. RSVP below.
**Election Night Watch Party Details**

body:
Don’t go to sleep on election night wishing you did more.

| | | | Friend,
---
Don't go to sleep on election night wishing you did more. That's the standard our Turning Point Action team is holding itself to. Right now, they're all gas, no brakes, and I couldn't be more proud of them. Everything this team is doing is more than just showing up right before November, because that's not what actually wins elections. It's about building real connections while reaching voters where they are, in their neighborhoods.
---

It takes years of preparation, with our door-knockers building relationships and earning trust. This is what my husband built Turning Point Action to do. Charlie wanted voting to become a habit for every America-loving patriot in this country, and our team is making that dream a reality, one front door at a time. Here's a look at what our team is doing on the ground right now: ✅ Hosting over 500 Super Chase events nationwide up until Election Day, activating people to chase votes in their own communities. ✅ We have trained and deployed 850+ full-time ballot chasers across key states, and the number is increasing by the day. ✅ Making sure voters in key states have a plan to submit their vote, through the work of our Chase the Vote team. ✅ Working day and night at headquarters so our field teams have everything they need to identify and reach every possible voter. ✅ Calling, texting, and writing postcards to voters, and hosting community events to get out the vote. ✅ Developing the "Freedom Ticket" as a personalized voter guide for patriots to use at the voting booth in key battlegrounds. ✅ Building permanent infrastructure in the new "Red Wall" states of Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire. When I see this machine at work, I see Charlie's vision growing stronger across America.

It's Chris.
**We have just 4 days left of this campaign.**
John Sununu has taken the lead in the polls thanks to over $67 million in GOP spending -- and they're taking over the New Hampshire airwaves.
We're running out of time to close this critical gap and keep New Hampshire blue.
**[Will you chip in $10 or whatever you can afford today to boost our grassrotos campaign and help flip the Senate?](https://substack.com/redirect/4a2b755f-14a7-4b6b-9513-87f00c93b017?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/4a2b755f-14a7-4b6b-9513-87f00c93b017?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I've been busy on the campaign trail, so I wanted to share a quick note with all of you:
As I've been traveling across New Hampshire -- spending time at community centers, town events, and campaign stops -- I've had a chance to hear directly from people about what's on their minds.
What stands out more than anything is how much people still care about their communities and are looking out for one another. That's something I've always believed is at the heart of our state, and I see every day on this campaign.
This campaign is only possible because of support from folks like you. I know firsthand that the only way to win competitive races is with overwhelming grassroots support.
**I feel so lucky that so many of you are standing with me as we fight for the Granite State 's values and future.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a2b755f-14a7-4b6b-9513-87f00c93b017?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. That means every single part of this campaign matters -- every door knocked, every conversation, and every contribution.
_National Republicans have made it clear they see this race as a top target._
If they're successful here, it would be a major step toward expanding their Senate majority and making it harder to champion the priorities that matter most to Granite Staters.
**[Will you chip in $15 or whatever you can today-- before our upcoming end-of-month fundraising deadline -- to help us make sure we have the resources to compete and hold this seat for Democrats?](https://substack.com/redirect/4a2b755f-14a7-4b6b-9513-87f00c93b017?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

With gratitude,
Chris

body:
Eugene won’t denounce it and now the Green New Deal’s biggest fan is coming to VA-07.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/NSG0dQw32mR?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Friends and Neighbors,
Yevgeny “Eugene” Vindman fled the Soviet Union as a kid.
But Yevgeny just announced he’s bringing _**Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez,**_ the face of the modern American socialist movement for a GOTV rally in Prince William County.
_**Think about that for a second.**_
In a district full of military families, small-business owners, and people who just want their electric bills and grocery prices to stop climbing, the best Yevgeny can do is fly in the congresswoman who once said the world would end in 12 years if we didn’t ban fossil fuels, championed the Green New “Scam,” and treats the border like a suggestion.
_**This is Yevgeny’s cry for help.**_
While Yevgeny is busy importing national progressive celebrities and dodging basic questions about not denouncing socialism, running this campaign the old fashion way: talking to actual voters across the district about energy, affordability, border security, and results.
_**He can have AOC. We’ll take the district.**_
Election Day is November 3. Every dollar we raise this week goes straight into the ground game that counters the circus coming to town Friday night.

Let’s send Yevgeny packing.
[**Chip in $25, $50, or $100 if you can.**](https://us.list-manage.com/Vygs_Y6OBu2?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)

One team. One fight.
****

**Republican Nominee for U.S. Congress****Virginia’s 7th Congressional District**

Plus: At the eleventh hour, the top GOP super PAC in charge of holding the Senate majority announced the launch of another seven-figure ad buy full of lies statewide.

That’s because Senate control hinges on this battleground race – and with just four days left to go, National Republicans and their corporate special interest backers are terrified.

**So if you’re ready to flip this seat, I’d really appreciate you chipping in what you can today to help my campaign keep up this momentum across the finish line.**

Washington is the warning Oregon cannot ignore: A voter can do everything right, place a ballot in the mail, and still have it rejected because the Postal Service stamped it too late. Across Washington, late-postmark rejections jumped 32% in the August primary. In some rural counties, the rejection rate quadrupled. **[Will you donate $10 to my campaign today to help me defend Oregon’s vote-by-mail system and make sure voters understand how to protect their ballots?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142503059/657162705/-569431239?refcode=261030-ontimers&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNDg2M2EyMS02NWQ0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hpE1qils2mqrL3Oy7vpYrftXvLF7_OOc7cMNHTnFcn8=)** **Oregonians have trusted vote-by-mail for more than 25 years. It is secure, accessible, and part of how millions of us participate in our democracy. Hey everyone, Matt here.
The Overton window has shifted, and I really need to talk about it again.
In my last article about political ethics, I wrote about Vivek Ramaswamy's ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged biological mother. The ad itself was disturbing. But watching people defend it as good politics or an acceptable campaign tactic showed how much our standards have changed.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/480629bf-02ae-4666-baa9-dbd6a3d17e38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [How Low Will We Go: The Death of Political Decency in America](https://substack.com/redirect/480629bf-02ae-4666-baa9-dbd6a3d17e38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Oct 21
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/480629bf-02ae-4666-baa9-dbd6a3d17e38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We have shifted in our intellectual and moral honesty. Democrats are quick to call Republicans unethical, and Republicans do the same to Democrats. Yet when we talk about campaign tactics, we increasingly skip the question of whether something is right or wrong.
Instead, we ask: Did the other guy do it? Can we use it as a political talking point? If they did it, does that mean we can do it, too?
Somewhere in that conversation, we stopped asking whether we should.
The controversy surrounding Mary Peltola's Senate campaign in Alaska is another example. And Democrats should be willing to call it out.
* * *
## Two Dan Sullivans on the Ballot
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d0a05155-cb67-4dbb-89de-dfc713049e91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Mary Peltola is a former Alaska congresswoman who lost her reelection campaign in 2024 and is now running for the U.S. Senate against Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan.
[The New York Times reported ](https://substack.com/redirect/7b1d5b53-c07e-4cb6-afb9-76658ed31335?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)that senior members of her campaign worked with Democratic operatives and personnel from the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, or DSCC, on a project to shape the ballot in her favor.
Part of that effort involved searching Alaska voter records for people named Dan Sullivan. Another Dan Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg, ultimately entered the race and appeared on the general-election ballot alongside the incumbent.
The apparent strategy was to confuse at least some voters into selecting the wrong Sullivan.
The investigation described internal communications, recruitment efforts, and discussions involving campaign aides and DSCC personnel. Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, said Peltola was "definitely aware," although she was not directly organizing the operation. Rios later tried to retract her statements, and the newspaper proceeded with its reporting.
Peltola denies knowing about the effort, and the DSCC denies involvement in recruiting the candidates. Those denials sit alongside the communications and accounts described in the investigation.
There is also money to account for. The pro-Peltola 49th State PAC reportedly paid approximately $87,000 to Wingspan Strategies, a consulting firm co-owned by an operative identified in the recruitment effort. The amount spent specifically on recruitment remains unresolved.
This was an organized effort to gain an electoral advantage by changing who appeared on the ballot. In the case of the second Sullivan, the shared name was the point.
* * *
## "Just Read the Ballot" Is Not a Defense
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ab028b39-d844-437d-92f6-55530d7531ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The response from some Democrats has been that the ballot clearly distinguishes the candidates. Read it carefully, they say, and you can tell which Sullivan is which.
That does not change the practice.
Somebody commenting on my Facebook post treated it as something funny, a **way to watch Republicans lose their minds**. But deliberately trying to confuse people while they vote is not a joke.
Let's say 99% of voters understand exactly what is happening. What about the other 1%?
The strategy does not require everybody to vote for the wrong candidate. It depends on enough people being distracted, rushing, or simply not paying close attention when they find the name they intended to select.
Alaska is a Republican-leaning state. For a Democrat challenging a Republican incumbent, small margins matter. One vote, two votes, a hundred votes. Campaigns fight over those numbers because they can change an election.
You can point to the middle initials, party labels, and other distinctions on the ballot all day. The ethical question remains: Why organize a search for somebody with your opponent's name in the first place?
I think deliberately engineering that kind of confusion should be illegal. We should certainly be able to agree that it is unacceptable without waiting for a court to tell us what our standards are.
* * *
## The Same Dirty Tricks in Ohio's 7th
In Ohio's 7th District, Congressman Max Miller has been attacking Brian Poindexter with claims about an extensive police record, including crack cocaine allegations and swallowing crack during a traffic stop.
But those drug allegations involved a different Brian Poindexter. The two men were born in the same year, but in different months. **The other Brian Poindexter is also Black.**
Miller put another man's record in front of voters as though it belonged to his opponent. That is a sleazy, deceptive tactic that depends on people accepting the accusation without noticing that the records belong to somebody else.
Democrats are right to call that out. But those same Democrats should be willing to condemn the Alaska ballot scheme. You cannot be outraged when a Republican uses a shared name to mislead voters and then laugh it off as clever politics when Democratic operatives exploit a shared name to confuse them.
The standard has to apply even when your own party benefits.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d41d093d-5ff7-4c7d-94c3-fc928d06d41d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
## Everybody Has an Excuse for Their Own Side
Republicans are furious about the Alaska story. Yet some of those same Republicans defended Ramaswamy's decision to use Acton's estranged mother against her, despite the documented history of childhood abuse and her mother remaining with the accused abuser.
Now some Democrats are defending the Alaska tactic with essentially the same argument: Get over it. We need to win.
That is exactly what I am talking about.
The objection disappears when the tactic becomes useful to our side. Suddenly, people who were demanding decency last week are explaining why decency is a luxury we cannot afford this week. Armchair moral justice warriors.
And there is always another example ready. Republicans did something similar somewhere else. Democrats have done worse. Somebody got away with it in the last election. The whataboutism that takes over the debate.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/cc2b9c6a-577b-44b4-b8cd-9e547166049b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [When Debate Dies, Democracy Weakens](https://substack.com/redirect/cc2b9c6a-577b-44b4-b8cd-9e547166049b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat) and [Dani Pajak](https://substack.com/profile/261941492-dani-pajak)| | *
---|---|---
| Jul 17
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/cc2b9c6a-577b-44b4-b8cd-9e547166049b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
How does any of that answer whether we should be doing it now?
If every unethical act becomes permission for the other party to do the same thing, the standard can only keep getting worse. Each campaign inherits the last campaign's worst behavior and treats it as the new starting point.
Then we act surprised when somebody pushes it further.
* * *
## We Cannot Keep Moving the Line
We have to do better.
The Overton window cannot keep shifting until there are no rules, no standards, and no norms we are willing to uphold. Those things are part of what allows this country to function.
The United States cannot run indefinitely on the idea that whatever helps your party win is acceptable.
The tactics described in the reporting about Peltola's campaign and Senate Democratic personnel deserve to be called out. So does Miller's use of another Brian Poindexter's record. So does Ramaswamy's exploitation of Acton's childhood trauma.
Our willingness to condemn bad campaigning cannot depend on which candidate benefits.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/578115f7-31d8-4ba7-af9a-1b551e4a430f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Fabricated Wedgewood Polls In Ohio Election Coverage](https://substack.com/redirect/578115f7-31d8-4ba7-af9a-1b551e4a430f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Oct 22
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/578115f7-31d8-4ba7-af9a-1b551e4a430f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If we want people to trust elections, we cannot excuse attempts to confuse them when they vote. If we want campaigns to tell the truth, we cannot defend misleading attacks because we dislike the person being targeted. And if we want basic decency in politics, we have to demand it from the candidates we support.
Somebody has to say that a tactic is unacceptable before it becomes another precedent everyone points to next time.
Because the window is moving so drastically and so quickly that we can barely keep up. Every time we excuse it, we help move it again.
I'll see you closer to election night to talk about where these races stand.

# PRESS RELEASE

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
October 30, 2026

**CONTACT**
Todd Cheewing
Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com

**LILY4CONGRESS CAMPAIGN FEATURES OVER 100 NEW HAMPSHIRE VETERANS WHO ENDORSE LILY TANG WILLIAMS FOR CONGRESS** **_With Election Day Just Four Days Away, Williams Highlights Strong Support from Granite Staters Who Served Our Nation_** WEARE, NH — With just four days until Election Day, Republican congressional nominee Lily Tang Williams is featuring more than 100 New Hampshire veterans who have officially endorsed her campaign for Congress in New Hampshire's Second Congressional District. The endorsements represent veterans from across the Granite State who have served our country and are standing behind Williams' candidacy.
[**SEE THE FULL LIST (CLICK HERE)**](https://us.list-manage.com/O2AzH8NA38D?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)
“I am deeply honored to have the support of more than 100 Granite State veterans who put their lives on the line to defend our freedoms,” said Williams. “As someone who grew up under communist tyranny, I understand just how precious those freedoms are. These brave men and women fought to protect the American Dream, and I will never stop fighting to preserve it for future generations.” Lily Tang Williams emphasized her commitment to ensuring veterans receive the benefits, healthcare, and respect they have earned through their service, while holding Washington accountable for fulfilling its promises to those who wore our nation's uniform. “Our veterans deserve more than empty promises from Washington politicians,” Williams added. “They deserve a representative who will stand up for them, fight for their interests, and always put America first. I am humbled by their trust and proud to have them standing with me as we head into Election Day.” Williams enters the final four days of her campaign against incumbent Democrat Maggie Goodlander, continuing to emphasize affordability, accountability, and protecting the freedoms that make America exceptional — the ones these veterans have fought so hard to protect.

**About Lily Tang Williams**
Born in China just before Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in more than a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.
**Paid for by Lily4Congress Committee** ###

Folks,
What a race it's been so far.
Since the start of early voting, our team and volunteers contacted more than 619,000 voters across North Carolina. And this week, I continued my Make Stuff Cost Less tour in Charlotte and Durham and felt the energy of a crowd ready for change and excited to cast their ballots.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/59604282-1ee3-4fe3-8ffc-bf5d31f5ffbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I launched this race last July because I knew that we could have better days ahead of us. And these past 15 months have shown me that North Carolinians agree. People all across the state and country are standing up and making their voices heard. They recognize that the chaos and corruption coming out of Washington DC is hurting their families and their communities and we have a crucial opportunity on Tuesday to vote for change.
That's the reason I'm in this race and why I'm still out here every day, talking with folks all across the state about how Washington can better serve them. Not the other way around.
Now, we're almost at the finish line.
**Tomorrow is the last day to vote early in person**. Find your early voting site [here](https://substack.com/redirect/c792c420-1dbb-4107-87c5-a2b3ec6ecb10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). If you've already voted, thank you! Reach out to a friend or family member today and help them make a plan to vote.
**Tomorrow is also the last day to register to vote if you haven 't yet.** In North Carolina, you can register and vote on the same day during early voting, but after that, you have to be registered to vote on Election Day. So if you haven't registered yet, find your local early voting site and register by tomorrow!
**Election day is on Tuesday.** If you can't make it tomorrow, polls are open on Tuesday, November 3rd from 6:30am to 7:30pm. Find your Election Day polling place [here](https://substack.com/redirect/c39665f6-14f9-41ed-b3e8-381171f02b77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
We have four more days to reach every voter in the state and make sure they have a plan to vote. **[Please, will you chip in $5 today and fuel our final organizing efforts so we can flip this crucial seat and take back the U.S. Senate to provide a course correction for our great country?](https://substack.com/redirect/59604282-1ee3-4fe3-8ffc-bf5d31f5ffbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/59604282-1ee3-4fe3-8ffc-bf5d31f5ffbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for being a part of this fight.
Thank you.

body:
[1]Talarico for Texas

We’re going for broke.

As someone who cares about taking back Texas, you deserve transparency.

When we talked about our closing strategy and our budget, we knew that
putting more resources into getting out our message and mobilizing voters
would make a significant impact on Tuesday. The race is going to be close,
and we can’t leave any stone unturned.

So late last night, I gave my team the green light to spend every dollar
we have — to get as close to $0 in our bank account as we can stomach.
Don’t wait until tomorrow or Tuesday — do it now.

Leaving a single dollar unspent and coming up short by a few votes would
be devastating. Folks put their faith in us to use every resource
available, and I take the responsibility very seriously.

We had to move fast because the sooner we can start spending, the more
Texans we can reach before they vote.

It was a risk. But I took a leap of faith and put my trust in you because
I have seen what this team is capable of.

have the resources to win without making any cuts to our budget. Every
dollar will be spent winning votes and getting us across the finish line
on Tuesday.

instantly.

this movement to leave a bunch of money in the bank and come up short.

Dream In the go-big-or-go-home collective consciousness of Texas, no
ambition is deemed too reckless, no daydream too wild. Save perhaps one.
It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that
the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32
years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the
race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen
by national Democrats as one of the breakout stars of this cycle, is ahead
of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the state’s scandal-plagued attorney
general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30.
A survey from mid-September, the ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll,
also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four
points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most
dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as
well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the
state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas
pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all
that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the
University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look
at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you
still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned
for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of
much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone
Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and
self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an
18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted
worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an
anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014.
Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of
defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to
Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations,
Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be
the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue
wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points
in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern
University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico
has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has
staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to
fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott,
meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been
unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated
Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to
Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for
dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such
optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where
idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there
is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has
built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level
Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the
Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have
written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for
more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule
in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W.
Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot
more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke
Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the
founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on
the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run
because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really
talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground
states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t
since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join
President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring
farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of
state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s
county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left
unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating
budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s
been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the
satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a
century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence
among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly
forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March,
with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican
four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr.
Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later
acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included
bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed
him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr.
Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans.
In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino
voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with
Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass,
and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans
who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of
Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness
of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog
party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across
20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi
of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the
Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande
Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a
place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine
Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by
the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at
the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many
markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms.
Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville.
“There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,”
she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s
campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr.
Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself
statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with
a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however,
Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an
effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that
quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later
renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six
biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr.
Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the
sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine
archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a
bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr.
Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the
riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which
Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a
century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and
Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other
American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created
instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic
concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business
executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in
an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating
with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,”
he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for
Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote
for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything
for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a
lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture
in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National
Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall
and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to
disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200
landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while
other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of
a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed
operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about
data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s
Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others
in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have
failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican
sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for
Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing
the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the
negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly
into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which
are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is
in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could
pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the
voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid
at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus
tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor
neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025
on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner
who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an
early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant
County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader,
Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican
Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex
school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a
State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in
2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated
riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the
2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that
saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for
midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A
few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020,
straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could
impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has
frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only
eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail
is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s
list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump
administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the
“suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent
shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its
Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for
Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is
because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the
margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get
it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t
win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful.
Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and
Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded
by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in
all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of
these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could
energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not
bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those
names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the
Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said.
Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic
enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also
doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive
for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you
get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a
winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a
“gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight,
but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,”
he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely
won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are
reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”'
