Mr. Talarico has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott, meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W. Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March, with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr. Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr. Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans. In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass, and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across 20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms. Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville. “There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,” she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr. Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however, Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr. Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr. Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,” he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200 landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025 on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader, Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in 2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the 2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020, straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the “suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful. Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said. Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a “gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight, but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,” he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”' You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

Greg Abbott has been caught in yet another lie, and this time, the receipts are coming straight from his own administration.
Last month, Abbott announced a so-called "pause" on data center permits, pretending to take action against the very corporations he invited into our communities with the richest tax breaks in the country.
**But new reporting revealed that Texas regulators approved 35 permits related to data center projects AFTER Abbott ordered his supposed pause. It 's crystal clear that this "pause" was a stunt meant to help Abbott score political points with the very communities he's already sold out.**
It's too late for Abbott to change loyalties now. He's married to monied special interests and has no commitment to the people of Texas, which is why he never bothered to enforce his own directive.
If Greg Abbott was committed to protecting Texas communities from the unchecked expansion of data centers, he would have taken me up on my call for a special legislative session to pass real laws that protect our communities and establish clear standards for how data center projects are approved and built.
While Abbott was telling Texans he was cracking down on data centers, his own administration was quietly allowing them to move forward.
Meanwhile, working Texans are left to deal with the consequences.
From Dallas to rural communities across our state, families have rightfully raised concerns about data centers threatening their water supply, straining our already fragile power grid, and moving into their neighborhoods without their input.
The question we should all be asking ourselves is **" When are we -- the people of Texas -- going to be included in the conversation on data centers?"**
My answer -- _when I 'm the Governor of Texas._ Texans deserve a seat at the table to decide IF and HOW data centers come into their community. Texans will get that power when I am governor.
**We can 't trust the arsonist to put out the fire. Greg Abbott took $22.5 million from data center interests, allowed 596 data centers to be planned or built across Texas, and then announced a fake pause to save his political career.**
_It 's time we object._
With Election Day just FOUR days away, we have a chance to put an end to Abbott's pay-to-play politics and elect a governor who answers to working Texans, not billionaire corporations.
**[I'm on the ground mobilizing voters, and we still have a lot of ground to cover. Will you please chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help us defeat Greg Abbott and elect a governor who will finally put Texans first?](https://substack.com/redirect/b6f50719-023f-4c71-a40b-33f9abfcd5f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Let's put an end to Abbott's data center madness.
-- Gina Hinojosa

body:
It’s a risk, yes. But I’ve taken bigger risks before.
#

Friend —
It’s Gabby. I had to make a tough call this morning, and I wanted you to hear about it from me.
Yesterday, our team showed me a plan to reach what might be an election-deciding amount of undecided voters in Michigan, Ohio, and Texas this weekend. The last weekend before Election Day.
The issue is, we don’t have the money for it yet. We’ve committed $10 million already, which is a significant amount for us. But this morning, I made a difficult decision.
I said yes anyway.
It’s a risk, yes. But I’ve taken bigger risks before. I ran for Congress, I fought back after I was shot, I learned to walk again, to speak again, one word at a time. I know what it means to refuse to give up.
Many of our races are close. A few hundred votes could decide who controls Congress and whether gun safety moves forward or backward for years to come.
So, I’m counting on you now. We need to raise everything we can to fully fund this plan before our end-of-month deadline tomorrow at midnight.

subject: what I admire most about Jane
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee
body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=12%2E6803%2Ev2N5mt)
It's Lily.
Jane and I have been friends for more than fifty years, which means we've been through just about everything, from protests and arrests at the steps of the Capitol to award shows and more _Grace and Frankie_ rehearsals than I could possibly count.
Sometimes the night ends with Jane sitting in my lap 😂.
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261030-ak.Kbs5jZ&refcode=em20261030-12&t=3&akid=12%2E6803%2Ev2N5mt)
Through all those years, one thing about Jane has never changed: **she never gets tired of fighting for what she believes in — for what she knows in her heart is _right._**
And you and I both know what is happening in our country right now is _not_ right.
Jane sees it. I see it. But instead of enjoying retirement like the rest of us, Jane is doing whatever she can to help elect the kinds of leaders who will fight for a dignified future for everyone who calls this country home.
**[Now I'm asking you to help: Jane's team needs to raise $50,000 in grassroots online donations before their fundraising deadline on October 31 at midnight. Will you chip in whatever you can to help them head into the final 4 days until Election Day with undeniable people power?](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261030-ak.Kbs5jZ&amount=5&refcode=em20261030-12&t=4&akid=12%2E6803%2Ev2N5mt)**
I'll admit it: even I've been amazed watching this movement grow.
_More than 250 climate leaders elected across the country._ Every one of those victories means another person in office willing to stand up to the fossil fuel industry and fight for clean air, drinkable water, and a democracy that actually answers to the people.
That’s the kind of future Jane and I have been fighting for since our _9 to 5 days_.
**And somehow — even with an egotistical bigot-in-chief doing his damnedest to drag us backward — that future is becoming more and more possible because people like you keep showing up.**
But we cannot lose sight of what’s ahead.
This year, Jane and her team have watched polluters and corporate super PACs spend massive sums against their endorsed candidates. We know the lies will only get louder, and the checks will only grow larger.
Over the next 4 days, we need to help these candidates knock on doors, make calls, and reach voters to compete with Big Oil and the powerful interests trying to drown them out.
That's not something Jane takes lightly, and neither do I.
**[So I’m asking you to help Jane’s team finish the election strong with a donation of any amount today. I’m immensely grateful for your support.](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261030-ak.Kbs5jZ&amount=5&refcode=em20261030-12&t=5&akid=12%2E6803%2Ev2N5mt)**

Let's keep this going.
Lily

**FRIDAY, OCTOBER 30, 2026**
**John Adams | Letter to Abigail Adams, October 13, 1775**
"Pray my dear cherish in the Minds of my Nabby and Johnny and Charly and Tommy the Remembrance of their Grand mamma, and remind them of her Precepts and Example."
John Adams wrote these words to Abigail after the death of her mother. He had seen how much their children's grandmother had contributed to their upbringing, and he did not want her influence to end with her absence.
We know that those we love will not always be beside us. Yet something of them may remain in the lessons they taught, the care they gave, and the example they set.
What do we carry forward from those who helped shape us?
**Pause.
Breath.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

---|---|---
**A SWEET GROUND INVITATION**
In Sweet Ground, we reflect on the people who shape us, the choices we make, what we must sometimes unlearn, and what we carry forward.
Now, I would like to hear from you.
Is there a moment from your own life that has stayed with you? Something a parent or grandparent taught you, a conversation you never forgot, a lesson you understood only years later, or an ordinary moment that turned out not to be so ordinary?
**Share your Sweet Ground moment in the comments.** A few words are enough. A memory, a story, even a photograph with a few words about what it means to you.
There is no right answer and no perfect story. Just something from your life that you carry with you.
I would love to hear it.

clean_body: | Friend, Imagine, you open your eyes on the morning of November 4th. Its the day after the election and you've awoken to a new day in Tennessee. You wake up to a Tennessee where power actually belongs to the everyday people who build this state and keep it running, not the billionaire corporate interests trying to buy influence. When we flip this seat , it won’t just be a historic upset . It will be the first time in twenty years that working families have a true champion in the Governor’s office. Here is exactly what we will do when we elect Jerri Green: ➡️ Fund our schools, not private vouchers scams: We will fully fund our neighborhood public schools and stop the corporate poaching of our communities' education dollars. ➡️ Lower the cost of living: We will crack down on price-gouging landlords and corporate monopolies that keep yourgroceries, utilities, healthcare andhousing artificially high while raking in record profits. ➡️ Fix our broken healthcare system: No more hospital closures in rural counties. We will expand access so that getting sick doesn't mean filing for bankruptcy. Now, imagine waking up to a Tennessee under Marsha Blackburn's extreme agenda :** private school vouchers gutting public education for good, rural hospitals locked out of Medicaid expansion while communities lose their last lifeline , and out-of-state billionaires writing tax policy while working families continue to struggle with the price of basic essentials like groceries and gas. Right now, Marsha and her dark-money backers are banking on one thing: that you’ll stay home and let them take the keys to the state. They know they can only secure victory when we believe change is impossible.But history isn't made by corporate donors or high-paid consultants. We know that real change is made by ordinary people who refuse to back down. We can win this, but only if we build the muscle to overwhelm their deception and their dark money. We need boots on the ground and resources in the field RIGHT NOW | | = | = Let’s imagine a better Tennessee ,together. # **El-Sayed quietly attends banquet with Hamas-loving activist**
Abdul El-Sayed **[attended a Dearborn banquet](https://substack.com/redirect/2e44b468-128f-4aee-8572-1b7def60e70b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** hosted by Osama Siblani's Arab American PAC alongside other Michigan Democratic candidates, deepening scrutiny of his relationship with Siblani, who has called Hamas and Hezbollah "freedom fighters" and praised Hezbollah's late leader as a "hero."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e44b468-128f-4aee-8572-1b7def60e70b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

# **Minnesota voter outreach to Somali community sparks election integrity backlash**
A clip of Minnesota Voter Outreach Director Melanie Hazelip explaining same-day registration and lax ID requirements on Somali TV went viral, with critics arguing the state's verification system, including non-citizen-marked state IDs and a "vouching" option allowing one voter to vouch for up to eight others, invites fraud.

| 2:25 PM * Oct 27, 2026 * 1.24K Views2 Replies * 2 Reposts * 18 Likes

* **The Minnesota Secretary of State 's office defended Hazelip's remarks** as accurate nonpartisan voter education, saying they'd been "misinterpreted and misrepresented," while critics like policy analyst Bill Glahn argued she should have emphasized citizenship requirements given the audience and timing.
* **The controversy follows broader scrutiny of fraud tied to Minnesota 's Somali community,** including a recent 30-year sentence in the Feeding Our Future case and a September indictment of a noncitizen accused of falsely claiming citizenship to vote in 2024.

# **North Korean hackers steal $6.3B in largest crypto heist ever**
Hackers linked to North Korea's TraderTraitor group **[stole approximately $6.36 billion from Binance,](https://substack.com/redirect/86b4cee1-9b5f-42de-85b7-fada088fed22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, across ten blockchains, with most of the theft occurring in roughly 20 minutes, according to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, which expressed "high confidence" in the attribution.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/86b4cee1-9b5f-42de-85b7-fada088fed22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Binance said deposits remain unaffected and withdrawals are temporarily suspended;** the exchange has recovered or frozen about $3 billion so far and pledged to cover all remaining losses using company funds and its reserve fund.
* **The theft surpasses last year 's $1.5 billion Bybit hack, also attributed to North Korea,** making it the largest cryptocurrency theft on record; one industry insider called it "the largest bank heist in human history," while Binance said it's working with law enforcement to identify and prosecute those responsible.

* * *
# **El Salvador deploys over 2,000 troops to Haiti after soldier kidnapping**
President Nayib Bukele **[ordered a surge of over 2,000 Salvadoran troops,](https://substack.com/redirect/88748e9f-59c2-4117-b00d-c20b79525533?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** into Haiti after gangs ambushed and kidnapped four Salvadoran aviation technicians serving with a UN-backed gang suppression force on Oct. 18.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/88748e9f-59c2-4117-b00d-c20b79525533?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Bukele rejected claims by an NGO that four burned bodies belonged to the missing men,** citing inconsistencies, and insisted on social media the deployment isn't an invasion, saying El Salvador seeks only to recover its soldiers and confront the gangs responsible.
* **The operation lacks a signed status-of-forces agreement with Haiti,** raising legal questions from officials like former Haitian defense minister Jean Dorneval, as gang violence has killed over 5,700 people in Haiti this year amid an ongoing security crisis since President Jovenel Moise's 2021 assassination.

| Peter,

Most Americans support abortion rights, and voters keep proving it at the state level.

In 2024, seven states — Arizona, Colorado, Maryland, Missouri, Montana, Nevada, and New York — passed ballot measures protecting abortion and the right to reproductive freedom.

[On Tuesday, abortion is on the ballot again in four states.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/142519327/657197378/610965683?sourceid=1151700&utm_campaign=27emcus-1007aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=ballot&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NmJkOTQ3ZS03MGQ0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EcMTzlAY1VKRPUXhMWB-oJLjCZF2EME3BGfKiYxaIbg=&emci=ad3f66e6-54d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&emdi=66bd947e-70d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=954237) Voters in Idaho, Nevada, and Virginia can protect reproductive rights.Missouri voters are fighting off a measure that would bring back a near-total ban on abortion:
* **Idaho's Proposition 1 would establish a right to abortion** and to reproductive freedom and privacy in state law. It would overturn Idaho’s current abortion ban, which is so extreme that doctors have left the state in droves.
* **Missouri's Amendment 3 would repeal the voter-approved Right to Reproductive Freedom Amendment** and ban abortion with extremely limited exceptions. Missourians voted to protect abortion just two years ago.
* **Nevada's Question 6 would establish a fundamental right to abortion** in the state constitution. Voters approved it in 2024, but it must pass twice to take effect. This is the second and final vote.
* **Virginia's Question 1 would make reproductive freedom a fundamental right** in the state constitution, including abortion, contraception, fertility care, and maternal health care.

Abortion bans cause real harm. Since _Roe v. Wade_ fell in 2022, a chaotic patchwork of state laws has emboldened anti-abortion politicians to escalate their attacks.

Patients are airlifted out of state for emergency care. They're turned away from emergency rooms. Some are forced to stay pregnant, only to deliver stillborn babies.

On Tuesday, voters in these four states can give millions of people the power to control their lives, their bodies, and their health.

**Peter, your support powers the Center's fight to overturn abortion bans and protect reproductive care for everyone, no matter the outcome on Tuesday.**

Thank you for being our partner in this work.

Onward,

Nancy Northup

If you know me, you know I don't put much stock in a single poll. One poll is a snapshot on one timeframe with one sample of voters - it's no reason to panic.
### **But this close to this election, there are no flukes.**
So I'm not going to mince words with you. This is a five-alarm fire for our campaign.
Donald Trump and the billionaires funding Susan Collins are reading the same numbers I am.
Up until now, Maine was worth a lot to them. Now, it's worth even more.

The Department of Justice is investigating CCTV video from Lewiston City Hall that appears to show dozens of instances of NGO workers -- operating as "interpreters" -- coaching illiterate Somalis on how to vote and even filling out ballots for them.
The shocking footage was obtained by The Maine Wire under the Freedom of Access Act and shows left-wing NGOs running an industrial-scale ballot stuffing scheme, using non-English-speaking migrants to obtain ballots and then instructing them on how to vote a party line ticket for Democrats.
"We review all evidence concerning complaints of voter intimidation and election interference, including the video from Lewiston's early voting at City Hall," U.S. Attorney for Maine Andrew Benson told _The Robinson Report._
"We will not tolerate threats to the integrity of our elections, and we look forward to working with the Attorney General's Office and the Secretary of State's office to defend our democracy," said Benson.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/39a18baa-2940-4707-b616-1b0d035d4340?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

When videos and images showing irregular behavior by the alleged Somali translators first went viral last week, Lewiston Mayor Carl Sheline quickly moved to block photojournalists from documenting the violations election officials would later disrupt multiple times.
Sheline, who spent $40,000 of his own money to win the $7,000 mayoral job, has been an unambiguous devotee to the narrow agenda of the Darod/Ogaden clan of Somalis that dominates the migrant NGO world in Lewiston.
Carl Sheline, seen here posing with Graham Platner, posted a notice limiting photography after The Maine Wire caught "translators" seeming to violate Maine law.
Sheline's bid to limit journalists' ability to document election shenanigans, however, did not cover the city's own CCTV cameras, which captured 140 hours of electioneering so tawdry it would have made Boss Tweed blush.
The CCTV video was obtained under Maine's Freedom of Access Act and covers the period of [early in-person voting](https://substack.com/redirect/ef5831f7-4b8e-4a6f-9f3c-5e18ee6692c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at City Hall, which began on Oct. 13.
Lewiston has been in the national spotlight since _The Maine Wire_ published [photographs by reporter Jon Fetherston](https://substack.com/redirect/b6433f7b-78e4-47c5-bfd6-446deb43252e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The photos raised questions about whether the dozen or more Somali NGO staffers working the early voting room were translating ballots or coaching voters on how to vote for Democrats.

Under Maine law, voters may request a translator, but there are strict rules as to what aides can and cannot do when it comes to assisting voters. Translators are not allowed to offer assistance but must wait until assistance is requested, and they are not allowed to influence voters' choices. The translators are not allowed to mark up a ballot, and they cannot approach or interrupt a voter who is already in the booth.
As is evident from the CCTV video, virtually every one of these rules was violated over and over again by a small cadre of political activists who can be seen shepherding illiterate Somali voters through the ballot-casting process.
After the national attention on voting irregularities in Lewiston, the city clerk began disseminating a printout informing the Somali NGO staffers of the rules.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ba66fb6d-31cf-4ab9-a308-a4d8ec70595b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The roughly 140 hours of security camera video only compounds concerns over fairness in Lewiston's elections, revealing that more than 200 apparently non-English-speaking Somalis voted with the assistance -- or coaching -- of the handful of Somali NGO staffers who were stationed throughout City Hall for almost the entire early voting period.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1d3cf0a0-c577-4398-a81c-6b056fe70ed5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
On Oct. 20, Fetherston said he had seen translators "talking to people and pointing at the ballots," and "a couple of people actually touching the ballots."
In another segment, a woman with a backpack appears to point to items on a voter's ballot while a second translator walks over and watches. Multiple other segments show the NGO staffers manipulating and even filling out ballots -- a clear violation of state law.
Two Republican candidates for local office in Lewiston, who've both been observing the election at City Hall, have also observed troubling signs that the election in Lewiston isn't on the level.
Janet Beaudoin, the Republican running against Democratic Rep. Scott Harriman in House District 94, [told the City Council](https://substack.com/redirect/be689e91-3710-4fa6-a58e-6d2be93105f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that an interpreter said he'd tell the person he was helping to vote for her if she were a Democrat.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/redirect/3ea55dc9-2438-433d-8ba7-260f44625703?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lewiston City Councilor Bret Martel, the Republican running in House District 95, told MWTV that 12 to 20 people came into that hallway holding issue signs. He said complaints had already forced him to remove a plain paper name tag and to pull the campaign magnets off his truck.
Fetherston said [three complaints have been filed](https://substack.com/redirect/9f1a7fd2-25f4-4536-8935-bc048e5647f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Lewiston police over the MPA's activity at City Hall and the conduct of translators.
A warden later told one interpreter to leave the voting area after the interpreter approached a newly arrived voter who hadn't asked for help, according to [City Clerk Kathy Montejo's account to Fetherston](https://substack.com/redirect/2f932878-5c37-470a-ac80-390fb76b1a3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
In response to the journalistic exposure of voting irregularities, the left-wing Maine People's Alliance staged a demonstration at City Hall -- a militant march through the institution which also appears to have violated Maine's statutes.
Maine law prohibits electioneering within 250 feet of the entrance to any polling place, and the MPA staffers can be seen on video marauding through City Hall with political signs. Those engaged in illicit electioneering include Democratic State Rep. Scott Harriman, who is also a candidate on the ballot in Lewiston.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/de53d55b-714d-49ee-807f-bcb2343616ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
One sign read "I am voting for my immigrant neighbors." The sign Harriman appears to hold read "I am voting for my community."
Secretary of State Shenna Bellows (D) said her office received complaints of "intrusive filming, photography and harassment of voters," and has said on privately recorded Zoom calls with left-wing activists that her office is investigating _The Maine Wire_.
With Election Day next Tuesday, the Maine GOP and Republican National Committee response to a brazen display of potentially illegal electioneering has been anemic. While the RNC has claimed to have observers on the ground in Lewiston, none have been seen. Meanwhile, the Maine GOP has sent four press releases this week with identical headlines touting party Chairman Jim Deyermond's recitation of Republican talking points regarding Troy Jackson.
On the other side of the aisle, Maine Democrats have held the governorship and both houses of the Legislature for nearly eight years. Yet despite the benefits of incumbency, they have grown increasingly bellicose in their bid to cling to power in Augusta.

In June 2023, then-House Speaker Rachel Talbot Ross (D), a business partner to Somali State Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D), told a Juneteenth event, "We should be storming the capitol," adding, "really, I'm serious."
The national reckoning over welfare fraud has, in Maine, centered on Lewiston and on one Somali-owned migrant agency with deep connections not only to the Maine Democratic Party but also to the very NGO staffers seen in the CCTV video hustling voters in and out of City Hall.
Following investigative reports from _The Robinson Report_ detailing welfare fraud allegations against the $5 million-per-year Gateway Community Services and its founder, Somali-American refugee Abdullahi Ali, Maine DHHS cut off MaineCare payments to the agency last December.
Although Gateway is now defunct, and Ali is on the lam in Africa, multiple former Gateway staffers continue to operate the political committee Ali and Gateway staffers formed after receiving lucrative no-bid contracts from the Mills Administration.
Those former Gateway staffers include Safiya Khalid, the director of the Community Organizing Alliance, who can be seen in CCTV footage orchestrating the movements of translators and voters, as well as Ahmed Aska Daher, a community health worker for Gateway.
How much of an influence could the Somali diaspora vote have in Lewiston, the Second Congressional District race, or even the U.S. Senate contest between Sen. Susan Collins and Graham Platner's replacement, Democrat Troy Jackson?
To estimate the total diaspora population voting in recent years, _The Robinson Report_ compared Maine's central voter registration data and other commercial data sets to a list of the 50,000 most common Somali names, which found an estimated 4,000 presumable Somalis registered to vote statewide, with approximately 1,300 of those voters providing addresses in Lewiston.
To vote legally in Maine, a person must be a U.S. citizen. For the voters in the video who were not born in the U.S. to be voting legally, they would need to be naturalized citizens. The presence of translators for hundreds of Somali voters raises the question as to how these individuals could be naturalized U.S. citizens if they don't speak English.
One possible explanation is that they are not, in fact, U.S. citizens, given Maine [Secretary of State Shenna Bellows' on-camera admission](https://substack.com/redirect/9bfcc6f8-88f8-4820-859e-5d3ce6c1736d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that she's aware that noncitizens are registered to vote in Maine.
However, there's another alternative. While naturalization normally requires an English test, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) lists a few exceptions. Under the 50/20 exception, an applicant who is 50 or older at the time of filing and has been a green card holder for 20 years is exempt from the English requirement.
Under 55/15, an applicant who is 55 or older and has been a green card holder for 15 years is exempt from the English requirement. Applicants who qualify for 50/20 or 55/15 still must take the civics test, but may take it in their native language with an interpreter they bring to the interview.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..JWtBhCfnq0WGlv4TnaAgPf4dHp2WndNOpUN4f7cV4wQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=222713896)
Under 65/20, an applicant who is 65 or older with 20 years as a permanent resident gets "special consideration regarding the civics requirement."
With Form N-648, an applicant who can't meet the English and civics requirements "because of a physical or developmental disability or a mental impairment" can request a medical exception. A licensed medical or osteopathic doctor or a licensed clinical psychologist must complete the form.
A voter who naturalized under one of those exceptions may be a citizen and still be unable to read an English ballot. Under section 672, that voter may ask for an aide.
So the more than 200 illiterate Somali voters seen on CCTV casting ballots with the help of one or more NGO staffers could well be naturalized U.S. citizens provided they applied for naturalization and were approved for one of those exceptions. According to USCIS data, the federal government hands out anywhere from 150,000-200,000 English proficiency exemptions in a given year.
In Maine, the rate of naturalizations has been modest: roughly 900-1,400 per year in recent years, according to the [Office of Homeland Security Statistics](https://substack.com/redirect/68ae8ea1-1ada-47d6-a356-7e64c40cb9cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Maine might be the only state where the Democrat Secretary of State openly admits that there are noncitizens registered to vote -- and then refuses to turn over voter records to the Department of Justice -- but it's not the only state where noncitizens on the ballot have become a political fight.
On Oct. 26, the Justice Department announced charges against 48 aliens in Pennsylvania, California, Florida, New York and Nevada for illegal voting, fraudulent registration and related crimes.
On Oct. 16, the department announced charges against 16 more in North Carolina, New York and Idaho. On Oct. 29, it announced 18 more indictments in North Carolina, bringing that state's total to 30 charged this year.
On Sept. 30, the department announced that a federal grand jury in Minnesota had indicted 10 foreign nationals, one of whom allegedly voted in this August's primary.
No charges have been filed in Maine related to noncitizens registering to vote or voting.

He said complaints had already forced him to remove a plain paper name tag and to pull the campaign magnets off his truck. Fetherston said with Lewiston police over the MPA's activity at City Hall and the conduct of translators. A warden later told one interpreter to leave the voting area after the interpreter approached a newly arrived voter who hadn't asked for help, according to . In response to the journalistic exposure of voting irregularities, the left-wing Maine People's Alliance staged a demonstration at City Hall -- a militant march through the institution which also appears to have violated Maine's statutes. Maine law prohibits electioneering within 250 feet of the entrance to any polling place, and the MPA staffers can be seen on video marauding through City Hall with political signs. Those engaged in illicit electioneering include Democratic State Rep. Scott Harriman, who is also a candidate on the ballot in Lewiston. One sign read "I am voting for my immigrant neighbors." The sign Harriman appears to hold read "I am voting for my community." Secretary of State Shenna Bellows (D) said her office received complaints of "intrusive filming, photography and harassment of voters," and has said on privately recorded Zoom calls with left-wing activists that her office is investigating The Maine Wire. With Election Day next Tuesday, the Maine GOP and Republican National Committee response to a brazen display of potentially illegal electioneering has been anemic. While the RNC has claimed to have observers on the ground in Lewiston, none have been seen. Meanwhile, the Maine GOP has sent four press releases this week with identical headlines touting party Chairman Jim Deyermond's recitation of Republican talking points regarding Troy Jackson. On the other side of the aisle, Maine Democrats have held the governorship and both houses of the Legislature for nearly eight years. Yet despite the benefits of incumbency, they have grown increasingly bellicose in their bid to cling to power in Augusta. Want to help The Robinson Report? Share this post on Facebook and send it to your friends! In June 2023, then-House Speaker Rachel Talbot Ross (D), a business partner to Somali State Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D), told a Juneteenth event, "We should be storming the capitol," adding, "really, I'm serious." The national reckoning over welfare fraud has, in Maine, centered on Lewiston and on one Somali-owned migrant agency with deep connections not only to the Maine Democratic Party but also to the very NGO staffers seen in the CCTV video hustling voters in and out of City Hall. Following investigative reports from The Robinson Report detailing welfare fraud allegations against the $5 million-per-year Gateway Community Services and its founder, Somali-American refugee Abdullahi Ali, Maine DHHS cut off MaineCare payments to the agency last December. Although Gateway is now defunct, and Ali is on the lam in Africa, multiple former Gateway staffers continue to operate the political committee Ali and Gateway staffers formed after receiving lucrative no-bid contracts from the Mills Administration. Those former Gateway staffers include Safiya Khalid, the director of the Community Organizing Alliance, who can be seen in CCTV footage orchestrating the movements of translators and voters, as well as Ahmed Aska Daher, a community health worker for Gateway. How much of an influence could the Somali diaspora vote have in Lewiston, the Second Congressional District race, or even the U.S. Senate contest between Sen. Susan Collins and Graham Platner's replacement, Democrat Troy Jackson? To estimate the total diaspora population voting in recent years, The Robinson Report compared Maine's central voter registration data and other commercial data sets to a list of the 50,000 most common Somali names, which found an estimated 4,000 presumable Somalis registered to vote statewide, with approximately 1,300 of those voters providing addresses in Lewiston. To vote legally in Maine, a person must be a U.S. citizen. For the voters in the video who were not born in the U.S. to be voting legally, they would need to be naturalized citizens. The presence of translators for hundreds of Somali voters raises the question as to how these individuals could be naturalized U.S. citizens if they don't speak English. One possible explanation is that they are not, in fact, U.S. citizens, given Maine that she's aware that noncitizens are registered to vote in Maine. However, there's another alternative. While naturalization normally requires an English test, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) lists a few exceptions. Under the 50/20 exception, an applicant who is 50 or older at the time of filing and has been a green card holder for 20 years is exempt from the English requirement. Under 55/15, an applicant who is 55 or older and has been a green card holder for 15 years is exempt from the English requirement. Applicants who qualify for 50/20 or 55/15 still must take the civics test, but may take it in their native language with an interpreter they bring to the interview. Under 65/20, an applicant who is 65 or older with 20 years as a permanent resident gets "special consideration regarding the civics requirement." With Form N-648, an applicant who can't meet the English and civics requirements "because of a physical or developmental disability or a mental impairment" can request a medical exception. A licensed medical or osteopathic doctor or a licensed clinical psychologist must complete the form. A voter who naturalized under one of those exceptions may be a citizen and still be unable to read an English ballot. Under section 672, that voter may ask for an aide. So the more than 200 illiterate Somali voters seen on CCTV casting ballots with the help of one or more NGO staffers could well be naturalized U.S. citizens provided they applied for naturalization and were approved for one of those exceptions. According to USCIS data, the federal government hands out anywhere from 150,000-200,000 English proficiency exemptions in a given year. In Maine, the rate of naturalizations has been modest: roughly 900-1,400 per year in recent years, according to the . Maine might be the only state where the Democrat Secretary of State openly admits that there are noncitizens registered to vote -- and then refuses to turn over voter records to the Department of Justice -- but it's not the only state where noncitizens on the ballot have become a political fight. On Oct. 26, the Justice Department announced charges against 48 aliens in Pennsylvania, California, Florida, New York and Nevada for illegal voting, fraudulent registration and related crimes. On Oct. 16, the department announced charges against 16 more in North Carolina, New York and Idaho. On Oct. 29, it announced 18 more indictments in North Carolina, bringing that state's total to 30 charged this year. On Sept. 30, the department announced that a federal grand jury in Minnesota had indicted 10 foreign nationals, one of whom allegedly voted in this August's primary. No charges have been filed in Maine related to noncitizens registering to vote or voting. * Watch my in-depth podcast about Gateway Community Services, the migrant NGO that became a taxpayer-funded arm of the Maine Democratic Party You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. **Friday, October 30, 2026 -**_****_
_**Iran** : Top U.S. commander briefs President Donald Trump on Iran attack plans. Senator Chris Murphy calls Trump's Iran war plan "insane." Qatari mediators return to Tehran for U.S.-Iran negotiations. NYT: U.S. oil companies take $130+ billion in profits during Iran war, Americans pay $147 billion for fuel. Small boat attaches explosives to tanker in Strait of Hormuz, sparking engine-room fire._
_**Palestine** : Israeli forces displace nearly 5,000 Palestinians in Hebron, settlers attack olive harvesters across occupied West Bank. Dockworkers at 110 ports across 22 countries strike against wars on Gaza and Iran. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu loses majority in Israeli election, rules out coalition with Arab-led parties._
_**Yemen** : Ansarallah claims six strikes on Saudi oil facilities and airports; denies accusation of attack over holy city. Saudi strikes kill 27 in Yemen._
_**U.S.** : Binance halts withdrawals after hackers steal $6+ billion in crypto. Axios: Fired Pentagon planner admits to leaking classified information on Iran, Ukraine to media, internal report says. Reuters: Pentagon suspects cyberattacks targeted refrigerators at military bases. Judge rejects Trump administration's Medicaid requirement for "medically frail" people. New Mexico megachurch endorses two Republican candidates, testing federal ban on church electioneering. DOJ issues new grand jury subpoenas in Alaska "spoiler candidate" probe. WIRED: Defense contractor connected personal AI agent to Pentagon network, exposing government data to third party. DOJ says FBI and ICE personnel won't serve as midterm poll monitors, but other federal agents will._
_**International:** Rapid Support Forces accused of attacks on civilian infrastructure. Ukraine strikes Russian refinery, violating promise to Trump. Finnish police launch criminal probe into Google data center. Christine Lagarde to step down as European Central Bank president. Albanian opposition storms parliament, disrupts session with smoke bombs and flares. Suspect in France shooting that killed one admits targeting people who "appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African." Icon of Mexican left Cuauhtemoc Cardenas dies at 92. Trump calls Brazil's election a "disgrace," declines to say if he accepts the result. Former El Salvador President Tony Saca released following corruption prison sentence._

* * *
# Iran
* **Top U.S. commander briefs Trump on Iran attack plans:** Brad Cooper, the top U.S. commander in the Middle East, [briefed](https://substack.com/redirect/304f2ab9-dad1-453f-9691-65a4145caef8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) President Donald Trump on military options against Iran at the White House on Thursday, alongside War Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Dan Caine, according to the Wall Street Journal.
* U.S. officials have warned Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the November midterm elections, while the Pentagon has moved additional air defenses, munitions, and supplies into the region, and relocated troops from vulnerable bases.
* The U.S. Army is deploying another Patriot missile battery to Israel amid concerns over interceptor shortages.
* **Senator Murphy calls Trump 's Iran war plan "insane":** Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations and Appropriations committees, said the Trump administration's plan to restart the war on Iran was "insane."
* Murphy [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/a2d2d7d5-533b-4397-b684-b8072f8ed4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a video of his remarks on X with the comment: "Some of us have been briefed on the war plan. And while I cannot disclose any details, I can say this: the plan is insane. It will not achieve objectives and will set off a new cycle of escalation."
* At an event this week organized by the Middle East Institute, Murphy said that the plan would "lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law."
* **Qatari mediators return to Tehran for U.S.-Iran negotiations:** Qatari mediators returned to Tehran for talks aimed at reaching a U.S.-Iran agreement, Reuters reported Friday. Qatar presented a U.S-approved draft plan to Iran on Sunday, but a senior Iranian official rejected the proposals as unacceptable.
* Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/26c05e16-8956-4ae8-8b0d-961c81f24271?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X that Tehran's conditions had been "repeatedly and clearly stated to the mediators," adding that "the carrot-and-stick approach has no effect on Iran," and that progress was possible only once Iran's proposals were accepted.
* Washington reportedly wants nuclear issues addressed from the outset of negotiations, while Tehran is demanding that the U.S. first end its blockade of Iranian ports and lift sanctions on oil exports.
* **NYT: U.S. oil companies take $130+ billion in recent profits during Iran war, Americans pay $147 billion for fuel:** More than 50 major U.S. oil and gas companies [earned](https://substack.com/redirect/01e8f879-87e5-42d8-861b-432ccfd9ce1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over $130 billion in profits between April and September during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, according to a New York Times analysis. Over the same period last year, the companies took less than $47 billion in profits.
* Comparing the same periods this year and last year, Exxon Mobil's third-quarter profits in 2026 more than doubled to $15.41 billion, while Chevron's nearly tripled to $9.92 billion, as soaring oil prices and disruptions to Middle Eastern refining capacity boosted earnings.
* Meanwhile, Americans have paid $147 billion for gasoline and diesel since the war began on February 28, equivalent to more than $1,100 per household, according to Brown University's Climate Solutions Lab.
* Despite the windfall, many companies are paying down debt and accumulating cash rather than expanding production or refining capacity. One oil executive, Valero Energy's chief financial officer, said that much of the surplus would ultimately go to shareholders.
* **Vance insists Trump will not let Iran conflict become a "forever war": **U.S. Vice President JD Vance [defended](https://substack.com/redirect/d90c72fa-9376-4026-b7e6-1014923444f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Trump administration's military campaign against Iran during a Fox News town hall in Fort Worth, Texas, after a Republican voter questioned whether the administration had fulfilled its promise to end costly foreign wars.
* "I understand the frustration about foreign misadventures in the Middle East," Vance said. "We've been involved in Iran in some form for seven months. The United States has been dealing with Iran for 47 years, and I promise you that Donald Trump is not going to let Iran become a forever war."
* **U.S. demands Iran cooperate with IAEA despite military attacks that halted inspections:** U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz accused Iran of failing to cooperate with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) at a UN Security Council meeting, telling Tehran's delegation, "Your lies are no good here," and insisting that the nuclear watchdog needed "answers, not speeches."
* During the meeting, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said that military attacks in June 2025 had forced the agency to suspend inspections and withdraw personnel from Iran for safety reasons.
* Grossi said that Tehran had previously agreed to allow inspectors into its Isfahan enrichment facility, however, "the commencement of the attacks prevented our inspector from going to the site."
* He added that the agency had identified no repairs or reconstruction at nuclear facilities damaged in the 2025 and 2026 attacks.
* **Small boat attaches explosives to tanker in Strait of Hormuz, sparking engine-room fire:** A tanker was attacked with explosive devices in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, approximately 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).
* A small boat approached the tanker and attached two explosive devices to its hull above the waterline, triggering explosions and an engine-room fire that temporarily disabled the vessel.
* UKMTO said that the crew extinguished the fire and resumed its journey, with no injuries or environmental damage reported.
* Separately, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said it had stopped two oil tankers in the southern waters of the strait after they allegedly switched off their navigation systems and attempted to travel through unauthorized routes with U.S. military support. It remains unclear whether the incidents are connected.

# Palestine
* **Israeli forces displace nearly 5,000 Palestinians in Hebron, settlers attack olive harvesters across occupied West Bank:**
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [continued](https://substack.com/redirect/99461130-b630-449d-97f5-cbd8c304a88b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their siege of the city for the eighth consecutive day on Friday, deploying military reinforcements, raiding homes, and forcibly displacing more families from Al-Jalda and Deir Baha. At least 4,969 Palestinians comprising 780 families have been [displaced](https://substack.com/redirect/cff5030a-326d-41fe-bd65-3cdf863fad9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including 336 infants, 441 elderly people, and 44 people with disabilities, Al Jazeera reported.
* **Nablus:** Israeli soldiers [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/17f7ce97-774d-407a-b0a8-db577f3176f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) stun grenades and forced more than 30 olive harvesters off their land in Al-Lubban Al-Sharqiya. In Burqa, settlers beat and injured a 36-year-old Palestinian, while others raided and vandalized a home in Al-Masoudiya, destroying its contents and cutting its electricity.
* **Bethlehem:** Israeli forces [assaulted](https://substack.com/redirect/5b2a21ea-c26d-4b8b-b1bb-9215deb7abac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinian olive harvesters and foreign solidarity activists in Abu Njeim, southeast of Bethlehem, forcing them off their land at gunpoint and arresting three harvesters.
* **Ramallah:** Israeli settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/40a550cd-0b0a-4944-8b21-f701cf46878c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olive harvesters and a solidarity activist in Kafr Malik and Al-Mughayyir, firing live ammunition toward Palestinian homes.
* **Jenin:** Israeli settlers [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/50688437-4929-47a8-bc9c-bb71579def7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Jaba, stealing equipment from an auto repair workshop, smashing the windows of three vehicles, slashing their tires, and stealing two sheep, according to the town's mayor.
* **Dockworkers at 110 ports across 22 countries strike against wars on Gaza and Iran:** Dockworkers at more than 110 ports across 22 countries on five continents are [striking](https://substack.com/redirect/01542563-7a24-4f66-aad5-f103523b042f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Friday, under the slogan "Dockworkers do not work for war," demanding an end to Israel's genocide in Gaza and U.S.-Israeli military attacks on Iran and expressing solidarity with Cuba, Venezuela, and Sudan.
* More than 25 trade unions are participating, with 24-hour strikes called in Italy, France, Greece, Turkey, and India, alongside shorter walkouts elsewhere.
* The campaign group No Harbour for Genocide estimates that more than $2 billion worth of cargo could be left idle, with participating ports handling 13.5% of global shipping.
* The group said it tracked 315 shipments of components for Israeli arms manufacturer Elbit Systems through 56 commercial ports between August 2025 and September 2026, all of which are expected to participate in Friday's action.
* The Palestinian labor movement endorsed the strike, urging unions to intensify boycott and divestment efforts against Israel.
* **Netanyahu loses majority in Israeli election, rules out coalition with Arab-led parties:** Israel's Central Elections Committee [published](https://substack.com/redirect/d5f70b39-dd20-4170-a1b5-d7ef76dc8b2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the final results of Tuesday's election early Friday. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority, falling from 68 to 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset. The main opposition bloc secured 48 seats, while the Arab-led Joint List and Ra'am won a record 19 seats combined. Neither major bloc reached the 61 seats needed to form a government.
* Netanyahu ruled out cooperation with Arab-led parties, [writing](https://substack.com/redirect/5d95eb51-face-4d86-896d-681f201b0a47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X that "it is forbidden to form a government with them," while his Likud party accused them of "stealing" the election. The Central Elections Committee rejected claims of widespread voter fraud, calling the reports "entirely unfounded."
* The official results will be presented to President Isaac Herzog, ahead of consultations on forming a government, while the new Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10.

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah claims six strikes on Saudi oil facilities and airports; denies accusation of attack over holy city:** Yemen's Ansarallah claimed six attacks on Saudi Arabia on Thursday, targeting major oil facilities, airports, and military positions.
* Ballistic missiles [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/c0b8f3ef-8ec9-4046-a529-cd072a50d0b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Ras Tanura refinery, Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq facility, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, and the Rabigh oil refinery, while a drone attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam disrupted air traffic, military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed. A sixth operation targeted Saudi military forces in Najran.
* Saudi-led forces said they intercepted and destroyed a drone over the Islamic holy city of Mecca on Friday, according to Saudi-coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki, attributing the drone to Ansarallah. Ansarallah [denied](https://substack.com/redirect/c6cc3ba4-036a-4e8b-9385-77c4318bfe22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) launching any operation against Saudi Arabia on Friday, calling the Mecca claim a fabrication.
* Separately, debris from two Ansarallah ballistic missiles intercepted above Riyadh caused minor injuries to one person and damaged a house and a vehicle, Saudi Civil Defense said.
* **Saudi strikes kill 27 in Yemen:** Saudi airstrikes on Yemen's Taiz province [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/b31d2127-392b-450c-adf3-2891a559ee60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 13 people on Thursday, most of them women and children, according to the Health Ministry in Sana'a. Ansarallah's Al-Masirah TV reported that three homes were destroyed.
* The Ministry said that another strike in Al-Jawf hit a crowded market and a nearby gas station in Al-Hazm, the province's capital, killing 14 people, including three children and two women, and wounding 15.
* Saudi aircraft also struck the central prison of the Western Coast Security Sector in Mocha district, on Taiz's Red Sea coast, wounding two inmates, one critically, according to Al-Masirah.

# U.S. News
* **Binance halts withdrawals after hackers steal $6+ billion in crypto:** Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/abb41467-2bce-45a1-81f0-6373d2c7ac78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that it suspended deposits and withdrawals after hackers stole about $6.3 billion in crypto coins. The company said that it would cover customers' losses. The research group TRM Labs said that it has "high confidence" that North Korea's elite hacking unit was behind the theft. On Friday, Binance said it had begun recovering assets and that it expects to allow withdrawals within two days.
* **Axios: Fired Pentagon planner admits to leaking classified information on Iran, Ukraine to media, internal report says:** The War Department's top military planner, Lt. Gen. **Brett Sylvia** , admitted to leaking classified information about the wars in Ukraine and Iran to two reporters over the last year, according to an internal report [obtained](https://substack.com/redirect/d78b4e92-e1f8-4eb5-aeaf-451a494eaa9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Axios. War Secretary **Pete Hegseth** [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/d78b4e92-e1f8-4eb5-aeaf-451a494eaa9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Sylvia earlier this week. According to a U.S. official, the firing came after Sylvia failed four polygraph tests and acknowledged leaking classified information on video. According to the internal report, Sylvia began leaking classified information to the media as early as June 2025.
* **Reuters: Pentagon suspects cyberattacks targeted refrigerators at military bases:** The War Department is investigating freezer malfunctions at U.S. military bases as cyberattacks, Reuters [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/7afcc8cd-cf40-47a6-9e99-68d0d2e95892?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In one case, the suspected attack caused food spoilage. Cyberattacks on more than 350 grocery stores in France earlier this month caused massive spoilage. U.S. Army investigators said they are collaborating with French authorities to discover more about "the refrigeration outages in Europe."
* **Judge rejects Trump administration 's Medicaid requirement for "medically frail" people:** Federal Judge **Richard Stearns** of Boston [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/471309ba-e945-4cad-9597-f19910bdff1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that the Trump administration's Medicaid guidance requiring chronically ill people to prove they can't work is "contrary to law." He said, "enforcement of an unlawful definition of 'medically frail' may lead to the disenrollment of otherwise eligible vulnerable individuals relying on Medicaid coverage for continuity of care." The ruling left intact many of the new Medicaid requirements--recipients must work, volunteer, or attend schooling for 80 hours a week to keep their benefits. These requirements take effect in January 2027.
* **New Mexico megachurch endorses Republican candidates, testing federal ban on church electioneering:** Legacy Church, a nondenominational church with nine locations in New Mexico, [endorsed](https://substack.com/redirect/96c702f6-b52c-4cd6-b24f-5bb92aaf0adb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**Greg Cunningham** , who is challenging Democratic Rep. **Gabriel Vasquez** in a district that Trump won in 2024, and gubernatorial candidate **Gregg Hull**. The endorsements may violate the Johnson Amendment, which bars tax-exempt nonprofits, including churches, from endorsing candidates. The church pastor **Steve Smothermon** told The Guardian that laws curtailing political speech are "null and void." The Trump administration is challenging the ban on church electioneering.
* **DOJ issues new grand jury subpoenas in Alaska "spoiler candidate" probe:** The Justice Department [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/7dd33271-974c-40a9-ae7f-966576f91729?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new grand jury subpoenas in its investigation of a "spoiler candidate" campaign in Alaska, the Associated Press reported. The subpoenas follow a Wednesday [report](https://substack.com/redirect/dbca4e1e-135b-45af-9b03-20b08627498e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the New York Times that Democrat **Mary Peltola** 's campaign wanted to spoil Republican Sen. **Dan Sullivan** 's reelection campaign by adding similarly named candidates to the ballot. Peltola's team allegedly recruited a retired teacher named **Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.** in the effort. President Trump said that Peltola "should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted." Alaska Gov. **Mike Dunleavy** ordered a state investigation into the matter. Peltola denied any knowledge about the alleged effort, calling it "just another distraction," and Sullivan Jr. has denied any contact with her campaign.
* The Times' main source for its story is Peltola's former campaign manager, **Elisa Rios**. Shortly before the publication of the story, Rios "retracted all statements made regarding the 2026 Alaska Senate Race," she told a reporter. "I am not willing to be a source for any story in any capacity."
* **WIRED: Defense contractor connected personal AI agent to Pentagon network, exposing government data to third party:** An Accenture employee working for the War Department [connected](https://substack.com/redirect/b211c872-58b2-447b-b57d-d281cb64fd6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their personal Claude AI agent to a government network used by intelligence agencies, WIRED reported on Thursday. The contractor linked their AI coding agent to a Pentagon network for unclassified information so that the agent could write and deploy code. The agent ran for two months with administrative access and appears to have sent login credentials and a map of the network to a third-party website that the National Institute of Standards and Technology has flagged as high risk.
* **DOJ says FBI and ICE personnel won 't serve as midterm poll monitors, but other federal agents will:** The DOJ [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3a2d6326-1fa9-4b2b-9926-f94e1a72134d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a court filing on Wednesday that ICE and FBI employees will not monitor the midterm elections next week. Instead, agents of the Bureau of Prisons, the ATF, and the DEA will. The disclosure follows a suit from the NAACP that sought to bar prosecutors and law enforcement from monitoring polling places. The DOJ said that agents of the Bureau of Prisons, the ATF, and the DEA will stand outside the polls to observe the scene, take notes, and interview willing voters. The federal agents will not act as law enforcement officials, the DOJ added, and will not carry firearms. DHS Secretary **Markwayne Mullin** said in September that ICE would not patrol or monitor polling sites but could be present "if there is a threat to that polling place or we're serving a warrant on someone that we have been actively tracking down."
