# Other International News
* **RSF accused of attacks on civilian infrastructure:** About 13 drone attacks [hit](https://substack.com/redirect/50dcf163-dacc-40b7-98b2-5a9a3b1b859b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several civilian areas across the Wad Al-Mahi governorate of Sudan's Blue Nile State on Thursday. The attacks, which local officials blamed on the Rapid Support Forces, hit a local market, a school, a health center, and several mines. The Sudanese government has accused neighboring Ethiopia of facilitating RSF attacks from its territory.
* **Ukraine strikes Russian refinery, violating promise to Trump:** Russia's Novokuibyshevsk oil refinery was [on fire](https://substack.com/redirect/a8b8f4fc-2503-46ca-9d0f-3fe008c8fa6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday after a Ukrainian drone attack, just hours after the Wall Street Journal [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/52040a01-b496-4ee8-8775-b41cdc00b2e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Kyiv had paused refinery strikes under pressure from the Trump administration. The Rosneft plant in the Samara region, which makes jet fuel for Russia's Aerospace Forces, can process 8.8 million tons of crude a year, equal to about 3% of all the oil Russia refined in 2024. It was last hit in August. The Journal reported that Ukrainian long-range units were told in mid-October to put refinery strikes on hold after Trump advisers asked Kyiv for a 30-day halt, citing people familiar with Ukrainian military operations.
* **Finnish police launch criminal probe into Google data center:** Finnish police are [investigating](https://substack.com/redirect/c6534120-238c-4876-89de-2cb3ab23dd90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) whether Google's local subsidiary Tuike Finland violated the Water Act and caused environmental damage at a construction site for a data center near Muhos, in northern Finland. A guilty finding could bring a substantial fine on the corporation. Google said that it will cooperate with the investigation. The construction site is part of Google's $15 billion investment in AI infrastructure in Finland. Electricity use across the country could rise up to 40% as a result of Google's data centers, according to an estimate by the national grid operator.
* **Christine Lagarde to step down as European Central Bank president:** Christine Lagarde [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/74217357-17b8-4ff6-ab4f-c9e0de6b42e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that she will leave the presidency of the European Central Bank on February 7, well before her term ends in October 2027. She said that she wants "the freedom of speech, the freedom of expression, and the freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy matters." She will preside over only two further policy meetings. European Council President Antonio Costa said the succession process for the position will begin immediately. Lagarde assumed the top spot at ECB in 2019. She is the bank's first female president, and its first leader not trained as an economist.
* **Albanian opposition storms parliament, disrupts session with smoke bombs and flares:** Sali Berisha, leader of Albania's opposition, [stormed](https://substack.com/redirect/b0335cff-224e-4119-adb9-5c16fcf05a83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) into a parliamentary session in Tirana on Thursday with other opposition members to demand Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation. The protesters deployed smoke bombs and flares inside the parliament. Berisha said that lawmakers "deserve tear gas, rubber bullets, cracked skulls, and broken bones, not the young people," referencing student protesters who have faced government repression. Prime Minister Rama has remained in high office for 13 years. He has refused to resign.
* **Suspect in France shooting that killed one admits targeting people who "appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African": **French authorities [charged](https://substack.com/redirect/f36d96b5-07c0-465b-9553-7432e33f633c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a suspect with murder and attempted murder in connection with a "terrorist" enterprise, following a shooting in the suburbs of Paris last week that killed one person and injured seven others. Most of the victims were foreign nationals. The suspect, who authorities identified as Kevin T, said that he targeted people "who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African." In a search of his home, police said that they found "weapons or weapon components, specifically a magazine, two pairs of brass knuckles, a steel bayonet, and a silencer." They also found a copy of the book "Mein Kampf."
* **Icon of Mexican left Cuauhtemoc Cardenas dies at 92:** Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, an icon of the Mexican left and the first elected mayor of Mexico City, [died](https://substack.com/redirect/b715f6b2-c549-4bc2-b11a-970629150248?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at 92, the Mexican government announced Wednesday. Cardenas, the son of President Lazaro Cardenas, broke with Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party in 1987 and lost the 1988 presidential election, which many analysts believe was rigged. He helped found the Party of the Democratic Revolution, and finished in third place in the presidential elections of 1994 and 2000. He became Mexico City's mayor in 1997. Upon his passing, President Claudia Sheinbaum called his role in Mexico's contemporary history "fundamental."
* **Trump calls Brazil 's election a "great embarrassment," declines to say if he accepts the result: **Asked Thursday about Brazil's presidential elections, Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/53c0b7ee-d23c-4bfc-97f7-ae143e41c3ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "I thought the election was a great embarrassment to the people of Brazil." He "didn't take sides," he added, but "take a look at the market, I mean their market went down through the floor." In the event, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva beat Flavio Bolsonaro by more than four million votes. The New York Times [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/c97f4e41-3ce6-4786-990e-c40c2044f18a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the Trump administration helped Bolsonaro and his family flee Brazil after he was defeated, crossing by land into Argentina under visas from Javier Milei's government, then flying by private plane to Ecuador and then Miami on Wednesday. Officials told the Times that the U.S. will likely grant the family permanent residency.
* **Former El Salvador President Tony Saca released following corruption prison sentence:** Elias Antonio "Tony" Saca, who [led](https://substack.com/redirect/5a145ae2-1927-4b17-850b-54e838206981?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) El Salvador from 2004 to 2009, was released from prison on Thursday. Saca, a member of the conservative Nationalist Republican Alliance, was convicted in 2018 of diverting and laundering more than $300 million from the state budget, for which he served ten years in prison. (The sentence was backdated to his 2016 arrest.) He is one of four Salvadoran presidents who have faced corruption charges. Prosecutors said he diverted funds for personal use and to benefit allies. A civil court separately ordered him to repay the state for the millions he stole.

Photo by Aris Messinis / AFP via Getty Images. Friday, October 30, 2026 -** Iran : Top U.S. commander briefs President Donald Trump on Iran attack plans. Senator Chris Murphy calls Trump's Iran war plan "insane." Qatari mediators return to Tehran for U.S.-Iran negotiations. NYT: U.S. oil companies take $130+ billion in profits during Iran war, Americans pay $147 billion for fuel. Vice President JD Vance insists Trump will not let Iran conflict become a "forever war." U.S. demands Iran cooperate with International Atomic Energy Agency despite military attacks that halted inspections. Small boat attaches explosives to tanker in Strait of Hormuz, sparking engine-room fire. Palestine : Israeli forces displace nearly 5,000 Palestinians in Hebron, settlers attack olive harvesters across occupied West Bank. Dockworkers at 110 ports across 22 countries strike against wars on Gaza and Iran. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu loses majority in Israeli election, rules out coalition with Arab-led parties. Yemen : Ansarallah claims six strikes on Saudi oil facilities and airports; denies accusation of attack over holy city. Saudi strikes kill 27 in Yemen. U.S. : Binance halts withdrawals after hackers steal $6+ billion in crypto. Axios: Fired Pentagon planner admits to leaking classified information on Iran, Ukraine to media, internal report says. Reuters: Pentagon suspects cyberattacks targeted refrigerators at military bases. Judge rejects Trump administration's Medicaid requirement for "medically frail" people. New Mexico megachurch endorses two Republican candidates, testing federal ban on church electioneering. DOJ issues new grand jury subpoenas in Alaska "spoiler candidate" probe. WIRED: Defense contractor connected personal AI agent to Pentagon network, exposing government data to third party. DOJ says FBI and ICE personnel won't serve as midterm poll monitors, but other federal agents will. International: Rapid Support Forces accused of attacks on civilian infrastructure. Ukraine strikes Russian refinery, violating promise to Trump. Finnish police launch criminal probe into Google data center. Christine Lagarde to step down as European Central Bank president. Albanian opposition storms parliament, disrupts session with smoke bombs and flares. Suspect in France shooting that killed one admits targeting people who "appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African." Icon of Mexican left Cuauhtemoc Cardenas dies at 92. Trump calls Brazil's election a "disgrace," declines to say if he accepts the result. Former El Salvador President Tony Saca released following corruption prison sentence. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Top U.S. commander briefs Trump on Iran attack plans: Brad Cooper, the top U.S. commander in the Middle East, President Donald Trump on military options against Iran at the White House on Thursday, alongside War Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Dan Caine, according to the Wall Street Journal. U.S. officials have warned Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the November midterm elections, while the Pentagon has moved additional air defenses, munitions, and supplies into the region, and relocated troops from vulnerable bases. The U.S. Army is deploying another Patriot missile battery to Israel amid concerns over interceptor shortages. Senator Murphy calls Trump 's Iran war plan "insane": Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations and Appropriations committees, said the Trump administration's plan to restart the war on Iran was "insane." Murphy a video of his remarks on X with the comment: "Some of us have been briefed on the war plan. And while I cannot disclose any details, I can say this: the plan is insane. It will not achieve objectives and will set off a new cycle of escalation." At an event this week organized by the Middle East Institute, Murphy said that the plan would "lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law." Qatari mediators return to Tehran for U.S.-Iran negotiations: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran for talks aimed at reaching a U.S.-Iran agreement, Reuters reported Friday. Qatar presented a U.S-approved draft plan to Iran on Sunday, but a senior Iranian official rejected the proposals as unacceptable. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf on X that Tehran's conditions had been "repeatedly and clearly stated to the mediators," adding that "the carrot-and-stick approach has no effect on Iran," and that progress was possible only once Iran's proposals were accepted. Washington reportedly wants nuclear issues addressed from the outset of negotiations, while Tehran is demanding that the U.S. first end its blockade of Iranian ports and lift sanctions on oil exports. NYT: U.S. oil companies take $130+ billion in recent profits during Iran war, Americans pay $147 billion for fuel: More than 50 major U.S. oil and gas companies over $130 billion in profits between April and September during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, according to a New York Times analysis. Over the same period last year, the companies took less than $47 billion in profits. Comparing the same periods this year and last year, Exxon Mobil's third-quarter profits in 2026 more than doubled to $15.41 billion, while Chevron's nearly tripled to $9.92 billion, as soaring oil prices and disruptions to Middle Eastern refining capacity boosted earnings. Meanwhile, Americans have paid $147 billion for gasoline and diesel since the war began on February 28, equivalent to more than $1,100 per household, according to Brown University's Climate Solutions Lab. Despite the windfall, many companies are paying down debt and accumulating cash rather than expanding production or refining capacity. One oil executive, Valero Energy's chief financial officer, said that much of the surplus would ultimately go to shareholders. Vance insists Trump will not let Iran conflict become a "forever war": U.S. Vice President JD Vance the Trump administration's military campaign against Iran during a Fox News town hall in Fort Worth, Texas, after a Republican voter questioned whether the administration had fulfilled its promise to end costly foreign wars. "I understand the frustration about foreign misadventures in the Middle East," Vance said. "We've been involved in Iran in some form for seven months. The United States has been dealing with Iran for 47 years, and I promise you that Donald Trump is not going to let Iran become a forever war." U.S. demands Iran cooperate with IAEA despite military attacks that halted inspections: U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz accused Iran of failing to cooperate with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) at a UN Security Council meeting, telling Tehran's delegation, "Your lies are no good here," and insisting that the nuclear watchdog needed "answers, not speeches." During the meeting, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said that military attacks in June 2025 had forced the agency to suspend inspections and withdraw personnel from Iran for safety reasons. Grossi said that Tehran had previously agreed to allow inspectors into its Isfahan enrichment facility, however, "the commencement of the attacks prevented our inspector from going to the site." He added that the agency had identified no repairs or reconstruction at nuclear facilities damaged in the 2025 and 2026 attacks. Small boat attaches explosives to tanker in Strait of Hormuz, sparking engine-room fire: A tanker was attacked with explosive devices in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, approximately 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). A small boat approached the tanker and attached two explosive devices to its hull above the waterline, triggering explosions and an engine-room fire that temporarily disabled the vessel. UKMTO said that the crew extinguished the fire and resumed its journey, with no injuries or environmental damage reported. Separately, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said it had stopped two oil tankers in the southern waters of the strait after they allegedly switched off their navigation systems and attempted to travel through unauthorized routes with U.S. military support. It remains unclear whether the incidents are connected. Palestine Israeli forces displace nearly 5,000 Palestinians in Hebron, settlers attack olive harvesters across occupied West Bank: Hebron: Israeli forces their siege of the city for the eighth consecutive day on Friday, deploying military reinforcements, raiding homes, and forcibly displacing more families from Al-Jalda and Deir Baha. At least 4,969 Palestinians comprising 780 families have been , including 336 infants, 441 elderly people, and 44 people with disabilities, Al Jazeera reported. Nablus: Israeli soldiers stun grenades and forced more than 30 olive harvesters off their land in Al-Lubban Al-Sharqiya. In Burqa, settlers beat and injured a 36-year-old Palestinian, while others raided and vandalized a home in Al-Masoudiya, destroying its contents and cutting its electricity. Bethlehem: Israeli forces Palestinian olive harvesters and foreign solidarity activists in Abu Njeim, southeast of Bethlehem, forcing them off their land at gunpoint and arresting three harvesters. Ramallah: Israeli settlers olive harvesters and a solidarity activist in Kafr Malik and Al-Mughayyir, firing live ammunition toward Palestinian homes. Jenin: Israeli settlers Jaba, stealing equipment from an auto repair workshop, smashing the windows of three vehicles, slashing their tires, and stealing two sheep, according to the town's mayor. Dockworkers at 110 ports across 22 countries strike against wars on Gaza and Iran: Dockworkers at more than 110 ports across 22 countries on five continents are on Friday, under the slogan "Dockworkers do not work for war," demanding an end to Israel's genocide in Gaza and U.S.-Israeli military attacks on Iran and expressing solidarity with Cuba, Venezuela, and Sudan. More than 25 trade unions are participating, with 24-hour strikes called in Italy, France, Greece, Turkey, and India, alongside shorter walkouts elsewhere. The campaign group No Harbour for Genocide estimates that more than $2 billion worth of cargo could be left idle, with participating ports handling 13.5% of global shipping. The group said it tracked 315 shipments of components for Israeli arms manufacturer Elbit Systems through 56 commercial ports between August 2025 and September 2026, all of which are expected to participate in Friday's action. The Palestinian labor movement endorsed the strike, urging unions to intensify boycott and divestment efforts against Israel. Netanyahu loses majority in Israeli election, rules out coalition with Arab-led parties: Israel's Central Elections Committee the final results of Tuesday's election early Friday. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority, falling from 68 to 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset. The main opposition bloc secured 48 seats, while the Arab-led Joint List and Ra'am won a record 19 seats combined. Neither major bloc reached the 61 seats needed to form a government. Netanyahu ruled out cooperation with Arab-led parties, on X that "it is forbidden to form a government with them," while his Likud party accused them of "stealing" the election. The Central Elections Committee rejected claims of widespread voter fraud, calling the reports "entirely unfounded." The official results will be presented to President Isaac Herzog, ahead of consultations on forming a government, while the new Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10. Yemen Ansarallah claims six strikes on Saudi oil facilities and airports; denies accusation of attack over holy city: Yemen's Ansarallah claimed six attacks on Saudi Arabia on Thursday, targeting major oil facilities, airports, and military positions. Ballistic missiles the Ras Tanura refinery, Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq facility, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, and the Rabigh oil refinery, while a drone attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam disrupted air traffic, military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed. A sixth operation targeted Saudi military forces in Najran. Saudi-led forces said they intercepted and destroyed a drone over the Islamic holy city of Mecca on Friday, according to Saudi-coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki, attributing the drone to Ansarallah. Ansarallah launching any operation against Saudi Arabia on Friday, calling the Mecca claim a fabrication. Separately, debris from two Ansarallah ballistic missiles intercepted above Riyadh caused minor injuries to one person and damaged a house and a vehicle, Saudi Civil Defense said. Saudi strikes kill 27 in Yemen: Saudi airstrikes on Yemen's Taiz province at least 13 people on Thursday, most of them women and children, according to the Health Ministry in Sana'a. Ansarallah's Al-Masirah TV reported that three homes were destroyed. The Ministry said that another strike in Al-Jawf hit a crowded market and a nearby gas station in Al-Hazm, the province's capital, killing 14 people, including three children and two women, and wounding 15. Saudi aircraft also struck the central prison of the Western Coast Security Sector in Mocha district, on Taiz's Red Sea coast, wounding two inmates, one critically, according to Al-Masirah. U.S. News Binance halts withdrawals after hackers steal $6+ billion in crypto: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, on Thursday that it suspended deposits and withdrawals after hackers stole about $6.3 billion in crypto coins. The company said that it would cover customers' losses. The research group TRM Labs said that it has "high confidence" that North Korea's elite hacking unit was behind the theft. On Friday, Binance said it had begun recovering assets and that it expects to allow withdrawals within two days. Axios: Fired Pentagon planner admits to leaking classified information on Iran, Ukraine to media, internal report says: The War Department's top military planner, Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia , admitted to leaking classified information about the wars in Ukraine and Iran to two reporters over the last year, according to an internal report by Axios. War Secretary Pete Hegseth Sylvia earlier this week. According to a U.S. official, the firing came after Sylvia failed four polygraph tests and acknowledged leaking classified information on video. According to the internal report, Sylvia began leaking classified information to the media as early as June 2025. Reuters: Pentagon suspects cyberattacks targeted refrigerators at military bases: The War Department is investigating freezer malfunctions at U.S. military bases as cyberattacks, Reuters . In one case, the suspected attack caused food spoilage. Cyberattacks on more than 350 grocery stores in France earlier this month caused massive spoilage. U.S. Army investigators said they are collaborating with French authorities to discover more about "the refrigeration outages in Europe." Judge rejects Trump administration 's Medicaid requirement for "medically frail" people: Federal Judge Richard Stearns of Boston on Thursday that the Trump administration's Medicaid guidance requiring chronically ill people to prove they can't work is "contrary to law." He said, "enforcement of an unlawful definition of 'medically frail' may lead to the disenrollment of otherwise eligible vulnerable individuals relying on Medicaid coverage for continuity of care." The ruling left intact many of the new Medicaid requirements--recipients must work, volunteer, or attend schooling for 80 hours a week to keep their benefits. These requirements take effect in January 2027. New Mexico megachurch endorses Republican candidates, testing federal ban on church electioneering: Legacy Church, a nondenominational church with nine locations in New Mexico, Cunningham , who is challenging Democratic Rep. Gabriel Vasquez in a district that Trump won in 2024, and gubernatorial candidate Gregg Hull. The endorsements may violate the Johnson Amendment, which bars tax-exempt nonprofits, including churches, from endorsing candidates. The church pastor Steve Smothermon told The Guardian that laws curtailing political speech are "null and void." The Trump administration is challenging the ban on church electioneering. DOJ issues new grand jury subpoenas in Alaska "spoiler candidate" probe: The Justice Department new grand jury subpoenas in its investigation of a "spoiler candidate" campaign in Alaska, the Associated Press reported. The subpoenas follow a Wednesday from the New York Times that Democrat Mary Peltola 's campaign wanted to spoil Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan 's reelection campaign by adding similarly named candidates to the ballot. Peltola's team allegedly recruited a retired teacher named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. in the effort. President Trump said that Peltola "should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted." Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered a state investigation into the matter. Peltola denied any knowledge about the alleged effort, calling it "just another distraction," and Sullivan Jr. has denied any contact with her campaign. The Times' main source for its story is Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios. Shortly before the publication of the story, Rios "retracted all statements made regarding the 2026 Alaska Senate Race," she told a reporter. "I am not willing to be a source for any story in any capacity." WIRED: Defense contractor connected personal AI agent to Pentagon network, exposing government data to third party: An Accenture employee working for the War Department their personal Claude AI agent to a government network used by intelligence agencies, WIRED reported on Thursday. The contractor linked their AI coding agent to a Pentagon network for unclassified information so that the agent could write and deploy code. The agent ran for two months with administrative access and appears to have sent login credentials and a map of the network to a third-party website that the National Institute of Standards and Technology has flagged as high risk. DOJ says FBI and ICE personnel won 't serve as midterm poll monitors, but other federal agents will: The DOJ in a court filing on Wednesday that ICE and FBI employees will not monitor the midterm elections next week. Instead, agents of the Bureau of Prisons, the ATF, and the DEA will. The disclosure follows a suit from the NAACP that sought to bar prosecutors and law enforcement from monitoring polling places. The DOJ said that agents of the Bureau of Prisons, the ATF, and the DEA will stand outside the polls to observe the scene, take notes, and interview willing voters. The federal agents will not act as law enforcement officials, the DOJ added, and will not carry firearms. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in September that ICE would not patrol or monitor polling sites but could be present "if there is a threat to that polling place or we're serving a warrant on someone that we have been actively tracking down." 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News RSF accused of attacks on civilian infrastructure: About 13 drone attacks several civilian areas across the Wad Al-Mahi governorate of Sudan's Blue Nile State on Thursday. The attacks, which local officials blamed on the Rapid Support Forces, hit a local market, a school, a health center, and several mines. The Sudanese government has accused neighboring Ethiopia of facilitating RSF attacks from its territory. Ukraine strikes Russian refinery, violating promise to Trump: Russia's Novokuibyshevsk oil refinery was Friday after a Ukrainian drone attack, just hours after the Wall Street Journal that Kyiv had paused refinery strikes under pressure from the Trump administration. The Rosneft plant in the Samara region, which makes jet fuel for Russia's Aerospace Forces, can process 8.8 million tons of crude a year, equal to about 3% of all the oil Russia refined in 2024. It was last hit in August. The Journal reported that Ukrainian long-range units were told in mid-October to put refinery strikes on hold after Trump advisers asked Kyiv for a 30-day halt, citing people familiar with Ukrainian military operations. Finnish police launch criminal probe into Google data center: Finnish police are whether Google's local subsidiary Tuike Finland violated the Water Act and caused environmental damage at a construction site for a data center near Muhos, in northern Finland. A guilty finding could bring a substantial fine on the corporation. Google said that it will cooperate with the investigation. The construction site is part of Google's $15 billion investment in AI infrastructure in Finland. Electricity use across the country could rise up to 40% as a result of Google's data centers, according to an estimate by the national grid operator. Christine Lagarde to step down as European Central Bank president: Christine Lagarde on Thursday that she will leave the presidency of the European Central Bank on February 7, well before her term ends in October 2027. She said that she wants "the freedom of speech, the freedom of expression, and the freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy matters." She will preside over only two further policy meetings. European Council President Antonio Costa said the succession process for the position will begin immediately. Lagarde assumed the top spot at ECB in 2019. She is the bank's first female president, and its first leader not trained as an economist. Albanian opposition storms parliament, disrupts session with smoke bombs and flares: Sali Berisha, leader of Albania's opposition, into a parliamentary session in Tirana on Thursday with other opposition members to demand Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation. The protesters deployed smoke bombs and flares inside the parliament. Berisha said that lawmakers "deserve tear gas, rubber bullets, cracked skulls, and broken bones, not the young people," referencing student protesters who have faced government repression. Prime Minister Rama has remained in high office for 13 years. He has refused to resign. Suspect in France shooting that killed one admits targeting people who "appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African": French authorities a suspect with murder and attempted murder in connection with a "terrorist" enterprise, following a shooting in the suburbs of Paris last week that killed one person and injured seven others. Most of the victims were foreign nationals. The suspect, who authorities identified as Kevin T, said that he targeted people "who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African." In a search of his home, police said that they found "weapons or weapon components, specifically a magazine, two pairs of brass knuckles, a steel bayonet, and a silencer." They also found a copy of the book "Mein Kampf." Icon of Mexican left Cuauhtemoc Cardenas dies at 92: Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, an icon of the Mexican left and the first elected mayor of Mexico City, at 92, the Mexican government announced Wednesday. Cardenas, the son of President Lazaro Cardenas, broke with Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party in 1987 and lost the 1988 presidential election, which many analysts believe was rigged. He helped found the Party of the Democratic Revolution, and finished in third place in the presidential elections of 1994 and 2000. He became Mexico City's mayor in 1997. Upon his passing, President Claudia Sheinbaum called his role in Mexico's contemporary history "fundamental." Trump calls Brazil 's election a "great embarrassment," declines to say if he accepts the result: Asked Thursday about Brazil's presidential elections, Trump , "I thought the election was a great embarrassment to the people of Brazil." He "didn't take sides," he added, but "take a look at the market, I mean their market went down through the floor." In the event, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva beat Flavio Bolsonaro by more than four million votes. The New York Times that the Trump administration helped Bolsonaro and his family flee Brazil after he was defeated, crossing by land into Argentina under visas from Javier Milei's government, then flying by private plane to Ecuador and then Miami on Wednesday. Officials told the Times that the U.S. will likely grant the family permanent residency. Former El Salvador President Tony Saca released following corruption prison sentence: Elias Antonio "Tony" Saca, who El Salvador from 2004 to 2009, was released from prison on Thursday. Saca, a member of the conservative Nationalist Republican Alliance, was convicted in 2018 of diverting and laundering more than $300 million from the state budget, for which he served ten years in prison. (The sentence was backdated to his 2016 arrest.) He is one of four Salvadoran presidents who have faced corruption charges. Prosecutors said he diverted funds for personal use and to benefit allies. # Math Matters
When the math does not add up, who pays for it? You Do! As Governor Phil Scott put it in his closing statement of the [gubernatorial debate on WCAX:](https://us.list-manage.com/cPo1DDPXEhM?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) “you have heard a lot of lofty promises [from Amanda Janoo]... but when you are Governor, the math has to actually add up.” And Janoo’s math never adds up. To make the point (that Vermont’s media should have been making for months), we did the math on just four of her campaign promises. And to cover the gap between what her income tax proposal raises, _**Vermonters’ taxes would increase, on average, by $2,100**_ to pay for just four of her policies. Not on “the wealthy,” but on the rest of Vermonters. _**Universal Primary Care**_ : Using Vermont’s medical inflation and the 2017 universal primary care report cited by the Janoo campaign, we estimate her plan to cost $610.8 million in year one. Janoo’s tax proposal raises between $114 million and $344 million. **Best case scenario, her promise is underfunded by $266.8 million; worst case scenario, it is $496.8 million in deficit.** The full program cost would require the legislature to increase income taxes by about 50 percent and it would have to impact lower and middle income households. This may be why she refused to say if she would raise taxes on lower incomes in the Vermont Public debate. _**Vermont State Bank**_ : Former Democratic State Treasurer called this proposal an “undue risk” to Vermont’s bond rating in 2014. When Vermont’s bond rating is downgraded taxpayers pay higher costs for projects. And according to previous testimony provided to the legislature, just to create the bank **would cost taxpayers between $50 and $100 million, before operational costs or potential losses. ** _**Federal Funding:**_ Amanda Janoo continues to say Vermont should reduce its use of federal funds. Vermonters pay federal income taxes. State administered programs like Medicaid, roads and bridge projects, nutrition assistance, housing, and low-income heating programs are all supported with more than $3.2 billion in federal funding. Even a modest **5 percent reduction in federal funds amounts to a $160 million state budget shortfall. ** _**F-35 Opposition:**_ On the Vermont Air National Guard, Amanda Janoo says, “if there is anything I can legally do as Governor to get them out of our skies, I’m down.” The Air Guard’s mission in Vermont supports the Leahy International Airport. Without the F-35s, there is no Air Guard. Without the Guard, the airport would look much different than it does today – and it would be much more expensive to maintain and operate. The Air Guard also directly supports about 1,000 great jobs. And the airport supports another 5,600. All together, this critically important economic engine **generates $62 million in taxes**. Much of that disappears without our Air Guard. __**The Bottomline: **__Janoo’s campaign promises would have real impacts on Vermonters already struggling with affordability. Just looking at these four proposals, and assuming her “fair share” taxes are implemented as proposed, the cumulative impact to Vermonters is, conservatively, about $679 million in **unfunded** policy and decreased state revenue. Divided by 329,000 (the approximate number of tax filers in Vermont), this represents a minimum of $2,100 more per filer, per year. And, again, that’s on top of the taxes she wants to levy on households making over $250,000 a year. **-Team Scott**

# Math Matters
When the math does not add up, who pays for it? You Do! As Governor Phil Scott put it in his closing statement of the [gubernatorial debate on WCAX:](https://us.list-manage.com/32uXg7CQJTj?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) “you have heard a lot of lofty promises [from Amanda Janoo]... but when you are Governor, the math has to actually add up.” And Janoo’s math never adds up. To make the point (that Vermont’s media should have been making for months), we did the math on just four of her campaign promises. And to cover the gap between what her income tax proposal raises, _**Vermonters’ taxes would increase, on average, by $2,100**_ to pay for just four of her policies. Not on “the wealthy,” but on the rest of Vermonters. _**Universal Primary Care**_ : Using Vermont’s medical inflation and the 2017 universal primary care report cited by the Janoo campaign, we estimate her plan to cost $610.8 million in year one. Janoo’s tax proposal raises between $114 million and $344 million. **Best case scenario, her promise is underfunded by $266.8 million; worst case scenario, it is $496.8 million in deficit.** The full program cost would require the legislature to increase income taxes by about 50 percent and it would have to impact lower and middle income households. This may be why she refused to say if she would raise taxes on lower incomes in the Vermont Public debate. _**Vermont State Bank**_ : Former Democratic State Treasurer called this proposal an “undue risk” to Vermont’s bond rating in 2014. When Vermont’s bond rating is downgraded taxpayers pay higher costs for projects. And according to previous testimony provided to the legislature, just to create the bank **would cost taxpayers between $50 and $100 million, before operational costs or potential losses. ** _**Federal Funding:**_ Amanda Janoo continues to say Vermont should reduce its use of federal funds. Vermonters pay federal income taxes. State administered programs like Medicaid, roads and bridge projects, nutrition assistance, housing, and low-income heating programs are all supported with more than $3.2 billion in federal funding. Even a modest **5 percent reduction in federal funds amounts to a $160 million state budget shortfall. ** _**F-35 Opposition:**_ On the Vermont Air National Guard, Amanda Janoo says, “if there is anything I can legally do as Governor to get them out of our skies, I’m down.” The Air Guard’s mission in Vermont supports the Leahy International Airport. Without the F-35s, there is no Air Guard. Without the Guard, the airport would look much different than it does today – and it would be much more expensive to maintain and operate. The Air Guard also directly supports about 1,000 great jobs. And the airport supports another 5,600. All together, this critically important economic engine **generates $62 million in taxes**. Much of that disappears without our Air Guard. __**The Bottomline: **__Janoo’s campaign promises would have real impacts on Vermonters already struggling with affordability. Just looking at these four proposals, and assuming her “fair share” taxes are implemented as proposed, the cumulative impact to Vermonters is, conservatively, about $679 million in **unfunded** policy and decreased state revenue. Divided by 329,000 (the approximate number of tax filers in Vermont), this represents a minimum of $2,100 more per filer, per year. And, again, that’s on top of the taxes she wants to levy on households making over $250,000 a year. **-Team Scott**

clean_body: | | | Peter, This is it. Four days. One weekend. That’s all there is until Election Day. Four days to defeat Trump, his billionaire-backed cronies, and all the chaos, war, and rising costs that they’ve delivered. Four days to elect the kinds of working-class champions that the Democratic establishment has told us were “impossible to elect.” Four days to elect people like Abdul El-Sayed and Will Lawrence in Michigan, Angie Nixon in Florida, Randy Villegas and Mai Vang in California, Bob Brooks in Pennsylvania, and Brian Poindexter in rustbelt Ohio. Across the board, our candidates are fighting for working families, not the billionaires — a home you can afford, health care you can rely on, a good job to support your family, and childcare when and where you need it. And we can win. We’ve been delivering political shockwave after political shockwave all year long. Working people are pissed off and hungry for real change, not just empty platitudes. But we only have this final weekend to turn that hunger into wins at the ballot box. And turning out voters during these final 96 hours takes a lot of resources to do. In solidarity, Team WFP P.S. | | | | | | Peter,
Election Day is Tuesday, and I want to spend the night before with you and all of our supporters!
On Monday, David Gallegos and I are hosting our Pre-Election Day Rally at the Rail Yards Market in Albuquerque. We’ll have mariachi music, good food, and a crowd of New Mexicans who are ready to bring leadership that works to Santa Fe.
**Monday, November 2
5:30 to 7:30 p.m.**
Rail Yards Market
777 1st St SW, Albuquerque
Mariachi Music & Food
This race comes down to who shows up. Monday night is our chance to thank the volunteers who have knocked doors for months, fire up the neighbors who are still deciding, and make sure every one of us has a plan to vote on Tuesday.
Bring your family. Bring a friend. And bring that neighbor who still hasn’t made up their mind.
Need your polling location? You can find it at [gregghull.com](https://us.list-manage.com/Gpkzb4H8ZJz?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810).

| | | Hi friend, it's Bill Clinton.

**I know you don't hear from me often, but I'm reaching out to you today for one simple reason:[There's too much at stake in this election for any of us to sit on the sidelines.](https://go.dscc.org/go/24212?amount=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20261030-BillClinton-BillClintonBackwardForwardFRRF26-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20261030-BillClinton-BillClintonBackwardForwardFRRF26-Pros-sl1&akid=27258%2E9716520%2E2YHd6I)**

In this election, like any other, we're faced with a fundamental choice: Do we, as a nation, want to move backward or forward?

For the past two years, the Republicans in charge in Washington have dragged us backward. They've threatened our institutions, attacked our rights, and enriched themselves at the expense of working people.

If we give them another two years of unchecked power, they'll cause more harm and drag us back even further. You and I know we can't risk letting them do that kind of damage to the country we love.

But it doesn't have to be like that.

On November 3rd, we have a chance to take the Senate out of their hands ‐‐ and if we do that, we'll restore the needed checks and balances that protect us from the kinds of things we're witnessing today. America will have a chance to turn a new leaf. **The path forward is clear.**

**[It all comes down to that fundamental choice: backward or forward? Hi there, it's Michele Tafoya!

If I were to take a guess, there's a 50/50 chance you may recognize me from a stadium's big screen.
If that's not the case, I get it... Let me at least tell you briefly about who I am and what I'm about anyway!

I should clarify first, no, I didn't make my career running for touchdowns or kicking game-winning field goals.

I worked as a sideline reporter in professional football for nearly three decades. Working in the sport for that long was a dream come true, and I wouldn't have wanted it any other way.
[Believe me, I know plenty of people who called me crazy for walking away from a career I loved. But life is short, and I was not willing to sit on the sidelines while everything I care about was on the line.](http://links.right-red.com/u/click?_t=7f2cc7f35be547959fee68a54bdac0d9&_m=ab174c61ee7149dbb4096f576d9eb187&_e=SWOLsTbLm0hr_P5wfqrnpgyVzWEyOwCAwYYWjSoTqMko14am62sSIffmjtgFCKkAYWdPtu_N4GLkuMy5MoMbKtBt5cmQEzG4icj1S3TrpIif4yJ91_lLbiGtHGHnWSmfFQ7qb4C61xI5fMAbuasTcEjsH8tDDU3zALSr2z3P79G5S0-yb2IkZzw2lCrEzYQp49DfuqasjBZwkDRjBP1PiYGDEytsb90KwI3Hlxvg-ZVhsnvczy4sZII8uCingb6U3vcFfSxHPM4MxuGpTqWdgISxarlQVzwQOyIus8yDzawRggWGktJm50MqmBbIsBIo7fVpr1oFgaRZ9ReXCvE8mUEUnsrn95y8gLc2jSDLckC6J5UMmPc2TwlIms6WSHtOMiu4rwn8q2s9sXZVAT9HZuKnDkznUFDWRHzWd9g-LL6rp4o8iCw-s0M1CJcRLYlpK3VNjw9rZwQkX6OH7fmpSdm_dkLTPYFeRED_21ZIMlUQSIO4-fSUYVfDWxU9ZHV0eZUWpE4sCcZwFA7Nd2TcetOHyThic8CKszk1qtbULbqwoDGvTIV7ltb1ajoljKdaCv4xG4kDL3xCWqqCLn0JvLIb-f5LhhJub1ZU5LK8BqMxSx695r9myB8t65mxkf7dnnLRuqpjHwIfxV9VYe1IhHVuyGL_MJZkFDetjraf5m7vtQIlQzjrUGEuSIKtjZU6Bpcyanw-p7r2G_vIVG53chFvaVoYrW8Zb2_lD6wKV-a_IObPocaceIWa6rGKrr1Au9iiW6MW2dQ9_E_oHFd9-p6Q7rQJo4Jw5QwFoUwzHME%3D)
I told myself before I officially launched my race for U.S. Senate that we had to be all in or not do it at all.

I burned the boats, and there's absolutely no looking back.
I will not be canceled. I will not apologize for values that are wholesome and good. And if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, that is exactly why I did it.

I want my daughter and every young American to know one thing:
You earn your place. You think for yourself. And you never let anyone put you in a box. That's the Minnesota I'm fighting for.
Parents who speak up are called transphobes. Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet. And women's groups are nowhere to be found.
This is not complicated.
Girls' sports are for girls, and boys' sports are for boys.

The radical Left has done everything in its power to infiltrate some of the most vulnerable minds in our society. I launched this run because just like you, I'm sick of the indoctrination and want to bring back sanity to our country.

It's going to be FAR from easy. Minnesota hasn't had a Republican Senator in nearly two decades! However, it's ripe for a flip....with the disastrous leadership of Governor Walz and the Democratic Party in the state, people are fed up.

It's going to take a grassroots army of patriots, just like you, to propel this movement of ours to victory and shock the world.

# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I didn't want you to miss this.
**A new poll shows me leading Greg Abbott, 49% to 46%.**
[****](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261030_2_254labs.F7Egqi&refcode=em20261030-2591&t=1&akid=2591%2E299639%2EzAbVbA)
Here’s why that number matters so much. In early October, we had cut Abbott’s lead to just 1.3 points. Then the polls started moving back his way. His lead in the polling average grew, and a lot of insiders decided this race was slipping away from us.
_**This poll was taken in the middle of early voting, and it shows us ahead.**_
What makes it remarkable is this: Greg Abbott has now spent $181 million in this race, five times what our campaign has spent. In the last month alone, he spent $35 million. **That’s as much as we’ve spent since the day we launched.**
**Spending: TX-GOV**
🔴 Abbott, total: $181 million
🔴 Abbott, last 30 days: $35 million
🔵 Our entire campaign: $35 million
He has outspent us 5 to 1. **But we’re outworking him, and grassroots supporters are the reason why.**
I’m not going to pretend one poll settles anything. Three points is within the margin of error, and Abbott isn’t going to stop spending now. The voters who decide this race are about to be buried in his ads. **We have to make sure they hear from us too.**
**That’s why my team set a goal to raise $3 million by tomorrow at midnight, which would bring us to $10 million raised in October.** As of writing this, we’re 93% of the way there.
If you’ve been waiting to see whether this race is really winnable, this poll is your answer. [**Will you make your first-ever donation of $15 today to help us keep this lead through Election Day?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20261030_2_254labs.NO0jKD&refcode=em20261030-2591&t=4&akid=2591%2E299639%2EzAbVbA)

We closed a 7-point gap once already. Abbott has spent $181 million trying to stop us, and today we’re ahead. Let’s take Texas back.
Thank you for everything,
Gina
_Our records aren’t perfect – if you’ve donated with a different email address, phone number, or by check, not all of your gifts may be reflected in our accounting here. I greatly appreciate all of your support in this campaign._

Election Day is just around the corner| | | |
---
| | | Friends and Supporters, **_It’s hard to believe we’re just days away from the 2026 election._** Voters have been telling me over the last few weeks what we believed all along - that this election is about more than any single candidate. **_It’s really a referendum on the future direction for America._** If you haven’t voted already, I hope you’ll take that belief with you to the polls on Tuesday. I knew when we started this campaign 13 months ago that it would be a momentous effort. But the kind of support and enthusiasm I could only hope for then has become very real today. Week after week we’ve been joined and buoyed up by a growing team of campaign staff, and just as important, by a core of volunteers that now numbers in the hundreds. And that effort by so many enthusiastic people out knocking doors, making phone calls, talking to neighbors and friends, is more important than all the extra money we could raise, and it’s what will make the difference for us on Tuesday. I am especially proud that throughout this campaign I’ve been running for office the same way you’d expect your representative to serve: by actually showing up and listening and talking with everyone. My opponent Michael Alfonso has NEVER been willing to do that. Our message about a responsible Congress that does its job, about fixing health care, about ending economic chaos, and about putting a stop to corruption is the same message I’ve been running on since day one. What you haven’t seen from our campaign is the ugliness and the negativity that is exhausting voters across the spectrum. As a result of that commitment to a practical, results-oriented campaign, Democrats, Independents, and Republican voters are all paying attention. Now, over the next few days we have our opportunity to close the deal. If you’re a WI-07 voter, I know you’ll be making a plan to vote on Election Day. But while we’ve made up our minds, remember there are thousands of voters out there who are only now making their minds up about who to vote for on Tuesday. Now is still our opportunity to make the case for those voters. So I’m asking you in these next few days to have as many conversations about this election as you can with voters across the political spectrum. Whether it’s making phone calls, knocking doors with one of our canvases, or simply talking over the fence or in town with friends, neighbors, and co-workers -- every one of those conversations that you can have are as impactful, or maybe more impactful, than any amount of advertising we could do. Thank YOU for being part of making the road to change in Congress run through Northern Wisconsin. I’ll see you all on election night. **_We can do this!_**
---
Fred

Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: Experience Matters. But What Kind?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/OsdJ39W0_aG?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/wWrAEOoncle?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Friends,Throughout this campaign, Mike Kelly has talked about his experience in government and his “deep knowledge” of Johnson County. OK.**But I think the better question is: What kind of experience does the next County Chair need?** Mike is an attorney whose professional career has primarily been in law.My professional experience has been built around **managing people, managing money, driving revenue, solving problems and being accountable for results.** I started my career in the hotel industry as a secretary in 1995. Within six years, I had worked my way up to Director of Sales and Marketing, essentially the chief marketing and revenue role for the property. In that position, I was responsible for driving all revenue, managing my budget, leading employees, setting goals and delivering results. The outcome? I was named Director of Sales and Marketing of the Year, for the entire corporation, the youngest ever to receive that recognition.Then I became a small business owner.And when you own a business, there is no department you can simply point to and say, “That’s someone else’s responsibility.” I have created budgets and cut budgets. I have hired, managed and developed employees. I have dealt directly with insurance, compliance, contracts, customer service, sales, operations and cash flow.**There is virtually no part of my business that I have not worked in directly.** My leadership experience also extends beyond business.As President of the Junior League of Kansas City, Missouri, I led one of our region’s largest and longest-running women’s civic organizations through the height of the pandemic, when organizations everywhere were being forced to make difficult decisions with incomplete information.All of those experiences have shaped how I view leadership.At one of the commission meetings, I heard Mike say something that has stuck with me:**“I trust staff, and if they say they need it, I’m going to give it to them.”** When I challenged that approach, he doubled down, explaining that he does not have HR experience, so he has to trust the people who do. Well, this is where Mike and I differ - I have extensive experience in HR functions from both my corporate and small business roles._Of course a County Chair should trust professional staff._**But trusting staff and providing oversight are not mutually exclusive.** The Commission’s job is to ask questions.
* Why do we need it?
* What problem does it solve?
* What will it cost taxpayers?
* What alternatives were considered?
* Can we accomplish the same goal for less?
* How will we measure whether it worked?
* Sometimes the answer should be yes.

**And sometimes leadership requires saying no.** That is what decades of managing people, budgets and operations have taught me. Good leaders rely on experts, but they also challenge assumptions and demand accountability.Mike talks about his “deep knowledge” of county government.But if deep knowledge of county government is the qualification, then I think voters should ask how anyone qualifies for the job before they have held it. Including Mike, as he had no previous county experience. More importantly, look at the results.Johnson County’s total budget has grown dramatically in recent years, and property taxes have skyrocketed.So this election presents voters with two very different kinds of experience.One is experience inside government.Mine comes from decades of **building organizations, managing employees, balancing budgets, making difficult decisions and being accountable for the outcome.****Trust is important. Oversight is part of the job.****We are four days away from this election. Please go vote. It matters now, more than ever,** Karen Crnkovich
Candidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

body:
Election Day is Tuesday! Here's what you need to know.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/14L8A1VP9rm?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

**🇺🇸 HERE WE GO, OHIO! 🇺🇸**

**Nov. 01 – Last day of early voting****Nov. 03 – ELECTION DAY TUESDAY
****6:30 A.M. POLLS OPEN****7:30 P.M. POLLS CLOSE**
###
---
|
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/xec83AK81Ke?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
|
---
| |

**Voting Locations**
**Find your polling place at** [ohiosos.gov/directories/find-my-polling-location](https://us.list-manage.com/q7lutP4LdWB?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
**Early voting location:** County Board of Elections

**Remember your ID:** Make sure you have an accepted form of photo identification before heading out to vote.
---
|
---
| |

**Know What’s on Your Ballot**

Election Day is about more than one race. Your ballot may include federal, state, and local candidates, judges, and issues that directly affect your community. Taking a few minutes to review your sample ballot before you vote can help you know what to expect, learn about the races and issues you’ll be asked to decide, and walk into the voting booth prepared.
Because ballots vary depending on where you live, we’ve provided links to the official Board of Elections sample ballot information for each county in Ohio’s 14th Congressional District. Find your county below to get started.
LAKE COUNTY — [View Sample Ballot](https://us.list-manage.com/3s1dFSPn8ag?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)GEAUGA COUNTY — [View Sample Ballot](https://us.list-manage.com/sVXDlm8eoHb?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)ASHTABULA COUNTY — [View Sample Ballot](https://us.list-manage.com/iMVsatqhpF8?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)TRUMBULL COUNTY — [View Sample Ballot](https://us.list-manage.com/BhJvDYap8eL?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)PORTAGE COUNTY — [View Sample Ballot](https://us.list-manage.com/qGMqVnmn3NS?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)MAHONING COUNTY — [View Sample Ballot](https://us.list-manage.com/7rNmWQGNWkJ?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)

---
|
---
| |

**Voting Tips**

**Pre-download your ballot.** Visit your county’s official sample ballot site before Election Day to see what will be on your ballot. If available, print a copy and make notes.
**Do your research.** Look up the candidates and issues throughout your ballot — not just the races at the top.
**Bring your notes.** Mark your choices, make notes, and bring them with you to the voting booth — it’s allowed and makes voting faster.
**Bring a valid ID.** Ohio requires voters to present an accepted form of photo identification when voting in person. Accepted forms include a driver’s license, state ID, passport, or military ID.
**Vote early if you can.** The last day of early voting is Nov. 1 at your county board of elections.

---
|
---
| | **THIS WEEK’S MISSION,
** should you choose to accept it.
**Hit forward. Pick five people. Done.**

You've officially done more for the campaign than most people do before breakfast.Good ideas spread one inbox at a time. Let yours be the first.

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

name: Rick Bennett
subject: Over $400 million is being spent tearing Mainers apart this cycle
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
The groups spending don’t answer to anyone here. They don’t care that Maine families are struggling with housing, energy, and health care costs.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Hi Peter, Over $400 million. That’s what ad tracers project will be spent in Maine’s elections this year. This is about what that money could do instead. It would cover ten years of Maine’s free school meals program. Or a full year of quality child care for 30,000 Maine children. It’s more than nine times what our entire state will receive in federal home heating assistance this winter. And the groups spending it don’t answer to anyone here. They don’t care that Maine families are struggling with housing, energy, and health care costs. To them, our pain is just another political opportunity to be exploited before the election and ignored after. **I am running to end this corruption.** At my press conference today, I laid out exactly what I’ll do as Governor:
1. **End dark money and require true disclosure:** full disclosure of the original source of large contributions, closing the loopholes that let anonymous spending drown out Maine voices.
2. **Require full financial disclosure by candidates for Governor:** so Mainers know up front who a candidate is beholden to.
3. **Reform lobbyist reporting in Augusta:** employment and contract agreements disclosed within 48 hours and weekly reports while the Legislature is in session.
4. **Defend the reforms Maine voters passed:** the ban on foreign government election spending and the $5,000 SuperPAC contribution cap, both now on hold while special interests challenge them in court.
5. **Push for an amendment to the U.S. Constitution:** using the bully pulpit to let states reasonably regulate money in politics.

I also called out what we all saw this week: the Maine Ethics Commission found that Bobby Charles took more than $45,000 in over-the-limit contributions and fined his campaign more than $22,000. My response: _“You can take the corrupt lobbyist out of the Washington swamp, but you can’t take the Washington swamp out of the corrupt lobbyist.”_ Here is the part that matters: I am the only candidate in this race who isn’t beholden to the system. Both parties and their candidates will do nothing to change it. **That is why we need you - not your money, but your voice.** Talk to five people this week. Five neighbors, coworkers, or family members. Tell them why you are supporting my campaign. That's it. Thank you for standing up to dark money.

Let’s give Maine the politics it deserves, together.

Rick
---

# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1233%2E127862%2E3XMNdW)
Folks, I’ve been hearing one question a lot these past few days:
_“Aaron, is it too late to pitch in?”_
Short answer: **no.**
Your $5 donation today absolutely makes an impact on a race as competitive as ours. **[Before I say more, can I count on your support?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261030_1_ak.gihaQp&amount=5&refcode=em20261030-1216&t=3&akid=1233%2E127862%2E3XMNdW)**

In the most recent public polls, about 1 in 10 likely Nevada voters said they were still undecided.
**In a race this close, that’s _more than enough_ to decide who wins this November.**
A lot of those folks are just now tuning in. They’re Googling my name, watching their favorite show, or catching the game. When they do, we need to be there with ads that show them who I am and what our campaign is fighting for.

Aaron
